questions.sdg_target: 1.3 Strengthen social protection via circular models
questions.kpi: Engagement in community-based textile recycling/upcycling initiatives
questions.question: To what extent does the company implement and sustain textile recycling or upcycling practices that generate local employment or income opportunities in vulnerable communities?

awareness.text: Map waste textiles or post-consumer materials available locally to establish a baseline; identify informal or low-income community actors (collectors, repairers) who could participate in reuse and upcycling.
awareness.source: Ellen Macarthur Foundation (Circular economy in fashion: building a waste-free, more responsible industry; ILO (2022) – Decent Work in the Circular Economy; UNDP (Towards a circular economy in Thua Thien-Hue province)

developing.text: Formalize partnerships with cooperatives or social enterprises and track year-on-year changes against the baseline for textile collection, sorting, and remanufacturing; monitor social and circular indicators (jobs created, tonnes reused).
developing.source: European Commission (New Circular Economy Action Plan); GRI 204: Procurement Practices (2016); ILO and International Co-operative Alliance (ICA) Joint Conference on Cooperatives and the Future of Work

leading.text: Scale inclusive upcycling hubs with multi-year targets for employing vulnerable groups; publish verified social and material-reuse outcomes; replicate models in new regions.
leading.source: EMF (Circular economy in fashion: building a waste-free, more responsible industry); UN Global Compact (Decent Work Toolkit for Sustainable Procurement); ILO (2023) – Social Protection Floors Recommendation No. 202

questions.sdg_target: 1.5 Build resilience for vulnerable workers
questions.kpi: Climate resilience measures in textile factories
questions.question: To what extent has the company assessed climate-related occupational risks and implemented climate resilience measures to protect vulnerable workers (e.g., temporary staff, garment workers in heat-prone facilities, etc?

awareness.text: Assess occupational climate-risk exposure (heat stress, flooding, vector-borne disease); map vulnerable worker groups and local adaptation needs.
awareness.source: ILO (2019) – Working on a Warmer Planet: The Impact of Heat Stress on Labour Productivity; UNFCCC (Global Climate Action Portal); ISO 14091:2021 Adaptation to climate change — Guidelines on vulnerability, impacts and risk assessment

developing.text: Implement workplace cooling, water access, early-warning systems, and emergency plans; incorporate adaptation actions in EHS procedures and training.
developing.source: ILO (2023) – Guidelines on Occupational Safety and Health in Hot Environments; ISO 45001:2018 Occupational health and safety management systems — Requirements with guidance for use; GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety (2018)

leading.text: Regularly evaluate climate-risk indicators and health outcomes; publish resilience KPIs; collaborate with suppliers to replicate heat-safety measures in value chains.
leading.source: ILO (Just transition towards environmentally sustainable economies and societies); UN Global Compact (The SME Guideto Corporate Sustainability); ISO 14090:2019 Adaptation to climate change — Principles, requirements and guidelines

questions.sdg_target: 1.2 Reduce poverty through fair wages & employment
questions.kpi: Percentage of textile workers earning a standard minimum wage
questions.question: To what extent does the company ensure workers receive wages that meet or exceed local living wage standards, contributing to poverty reduction?

awareness.text: Benchmark wages against statutory minimums and credible living-wage estimates; identify gaps for vulnerable or contract workers.
awareness.source: ILO (2022) – Global Wage Report 2022–23; UN Global Compact Living Wage Analysis Tool; GRI 202: Market Presence 2016

developing.text: Adopt and disclose a formal living-wage policy; include living-wage clauses in supplier codes; monitor pay equity across gender and job levels.
developing.source: OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises on Responsible Business Conduct; ILO – Decent Work Indicators; GRI 405: DIVERSITY AND EQUAL OPPORTUNITY 2016

leading.text: Publicly report wage ratios, living-wage coverage, and progress; collaborate with industry peers to raise wage floors across the sector.
leading.source: UN Global Combact (Achieving the Living Wage Ambition: Reference Sheet and Implementation Guidance); GRI 2 + 202 (2021) – General Disclosures & Market Presence; Global Living Wage Coalition

questions.sdg_target: 1.4 Ensure access to financial services
questions.kpi: Access to microfinance or financial literacy programs
questions.question: To what extent does the company continuosly provide employees with access to financial literacy programs, savings schemes, or partnerships that improve financial security for low-income workers?

awareness.text: Evaluate workers’ access to financial tools and vulnerabilities (indebtedness, lack of savings); identify relevant partners (credit unions, NGOs, digital-finance providers).
awareness.source: UNCDF (Inclusive Digital Economies); OECD/INFE TOOLKIT FOR MEASURING FINANCIAL LITERACY AND FINANCIAL INCLUSION 2022); ILO 2019 (Inclusive Finance for Workers brochure)

developing.text: Introduce on-site financial-literacy sessions, voluntary savings accounts, and access to fair-cost micro-credit or insurance; monitor participation and impacts.
developing.source: UNDP 2021 (Financial inclusion as a key for poverty reduction); ILO (Social Finance Programme); GRI 401: Employment 2016

leading.text: Integrate financial-well-being KPIs (e.g., % employees with savings accounts, reduction in payday-loan usage); scale programs through local partnerships.
leading.source: UN Global Compact – SDG Ambition Benchmark; 2022 OECD/INFE Toolkit for Measuring Financial Literacy and Financial Inclusion; ILO (Sustainable Financing of Social Protection)

questions.sdg_target: 2.5 Maintain genetic diversity of seeds, cultivated plants
questions.kpi: % of agricultural waste used
questions.question: To what extent has the company increased the use of fibers from diverse agricultural by-products over time, reducing dependence on single raw materials and supporting agricultural biodiversity

awareness.text: Identify opportunities to substitute conventional mono-crop fibers (e.g., cotton) with agricultural residues and diverse plant fibers such as banana, hemp, or pineapple. Assess potential biodiversity benefits and local availability.
awareness.source: FAO (2023) – State of the World’s Biodiversity for Food and Agriculture; Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2021) – Circular Design for Fashion; ISO 59004:2024 Circular economy — Vocabulary, principles and guidance for implementation

developing.text: Pilot product lines using diverse agricultural by-products; establish traceability for fiber origins; evaluate life-cycle impacts and farmer benefits.
developing.source: FAO 2021 (Selecting value chains for sustainable food value chain development); GRI 301: Materials Sustainability Reporting Requirements; EMF (Circular economy in fashion: building a waste-free, more responsible industry)

leading.text: Scale production using regenerative, biodiversity-friendly fiber systems; publish biodiversity and livelihood outcomes from agricultural by-product sourcing.
leading.source: FAO 2022 (Framework for Action on Biodiversity for Food and Agriculture); EEA (The benefits to biodiversity of a strong circular economy); GRI 304: Biodiversity (2016)

questions.sdg_target: 2.4 Ensure sustainable food production systems and implement resilient agricultural practices
questions.kpi: Support of ecosystem restoration
questions.question: Has the company adopted and progressively expanded sourcing practices (e.g., certified cotton, regenerative agriculture, biodiversity standards) that contribute to restoring or maintaining healthy agricultural ecosystems in its supply chain regions?

awareness.text: Map agricultural inputs and identify ecosystems under stress; evaluate certification options (e.g., organic, regenerative, Rainforest Alliance, or Fairtrade).
awareness.source: FAO (Sustainable Food and Agriculture); UNEP (2021) – Becoming #GenerationRestoration: Ecosystem Restoration for People, Nature and Climate; ISO 14055-1:2017 Environmental management — Guidelines for establishing good practices for combatting land degradation and desertification

developing.text: Adopt and verify sustainable agriculture standards across supply chains; integrate regenerative principles (cover cropping, minimal tillage, soil organic matter improvement).
developing.source: ROC 2023 (Framework for Regenerative Organic Certified); GRI 308: SUPPLIER ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT 2016 ; UN Global Compact (The Ten Principles)

leading.text: Co-develop regenerative-agriculture pilots with suppliers and farmers; measure ecosystem recovery and GHG reduction; report results via GRI and science-based targets.
leading.source: FAO 2023 (Agroecology Knowledge Hub); UNEP 2021 (Rethinking Food Systems); UNEP (Greening the Blue Report 2022); Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi, 2023) – Forest, Land and Agriculture Guidance (FLAG)

questions.sdg_target: 2.3 Double the productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers
questions.kpi: % increase in sourcing from small-scale farmers or cooperatives producing natural fibers
questions.question: To what extent does the company source agricultural fibers (e.g., cotton, hemp, flax) from small-scale farmers or cooperatives, thereby improving livelihoods and market access for vulnerable producers?

awareness.text: Identify existing suppliers’ scale and ownership type (smallholder, cooperative); analyze procurement concentration and local development impact.
awareness.source: FAO (2021) – Family Farming Knowledge Platform; ILO 2024 ( Highlights on the cooperative, social and solidarity economy); UN Global Compact (Decent Work Toolkit for Sustainable Procurement)

developing.text: Source from verified smallholder cooperatives; offer long-term contracts or prepayment models; build local capacity for sustainable fiber cultivation.
developing.source: FAO (Empowering smallholders, family farms and youth); GRI 204: PROCUREMENT PRACTICES 2016; FAO (Responsible agriculture supply chains)

leading.text: Report smallholder sourcing share (% of procurement); provide technical and financial support for productivity and resilience; co-create inclusive circular value chains.
leading.source: UN Global Compact(Forward Faster); FAO (The State of Food and Agriculture 2023); GRI 203: Indirect Economic Impacts 2016

questions.sdg_target: 2.1 Nutritious and sufficient food for all
questions.kpi: % of employees provided access to affordable and nutritious meals at the workplace
questions.question: To what extent does the company provide affordable and nutritious food options for employees (e.g., canteen meals, subsidised food programs) at the workplace?

awareness.text: Assess employee food access, dietary diversity, and affordability; evaluate workplace nutrition options and local food security context.
awareness.source: FAO (The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World); WHO (2020) – Healthy Diets; ILO 2005 (FOOD AT WORK)

developing.text: Provide healthy canteen meals or food vouchers; integrate nutrition education into wellness programs; measure participation and satisfaction.
developing.source: UN Global Compact (Integrate the Food and Agriculture Business Principles); GRI 403: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY 2018; FAO 2021 (FAO’s work in nutrition: Raising levels of nutrition for all)

leading.text: Implement verified workplace-nutrition certification or SDG-aligned employee wellness benchmarks; disclose food security and nutrition performance publicly.
leading.source: WHO (Healthy workplaces:a model for action); UN Global Compact (SDG AMBITION BENCHMARKS); GRI 401: Employment (2016)

questions.sdg_target: 3.9 Reduce exposure through circularity
questions.kpi: % of recycled materials certified safe for health
questions.question: To what extent does the company verify and progressively increase the share of recycled or upcycled textile materials used in production are tested and certified to be free from harmful substances for workers and consumers?

awareness.text: Map existing recycled/upcycled inputs, identify potential contaminants (e.g., PFAS, azo dyes, heavy metals), and review globally recognized safety certifications for textiles.
awareness.source: OEKO-TEX® STANDARD 100: the original safety standard; UNEP (Chemicals and pollution action); OECD (Assessment of chemicals)

developing.text: Require chemical testing for all recycled/upcycled fibers; adopt supplier verification procedures; ensure compliance with recognized safety standards (e.g., OEKO-TEX, ZDHC MRSL).
developing.source: MRSL (Safer chemicals A good start transforms the end result.); OECD (Chemical safety and biosafety); GRI 301: Materials

leading.text: Set validated targets for certified-safe circular inputs; conduct third-party audits; publicly disclose toxic-free recycled-material performance.
leading.source: OEKO-TEX® STeP: Responsible production for people and planet.; UNEP (Global Chemicals Outlook); GRI 102: Climate Change and GRI 103: Energy standards

questions.sdg_target: 3.9 Reduce exposure to hazardous chemicals
questions.kpi: % reduction in use of hazardous dyes and treatments
questions.question: Has the company phased out or significantly reduced hazardous chemicals in dyeing, finishing, and other processes by adopting safer, non-toxic alternatives?

awareness.text: Identify hazardous chemicals in processes, review regulatory lists, and map toxic hotspots.
awareness.source: UNEP SAICM - Global Framework on Chemicals; OECD (Substitution and Alternatives Assessment Toolbox (SAAToolbox) for chemicals and nanomaterials); ZDHC (Paving the way for sustainable chemical management within the fashion industry)

developing.text: Adopt safer alternatives; phase out PFAS, chlorinated solvents, azo dyes, etc.; expand chemical inventories and conduct risk assessments.
developing.source: ISO 14001:2015 – Environmental Management Systems; OECD (Guidance on Key Considerations for the Identification and Selection of Safer Chemical Alternatives); GRI 306: Waste (2020)

leading.text: Implement a zero-toxic chemical strategy; publish chemical-reduction KPIs; certify facilities through ZDHC or OEKO-TEX STeP.
leading.source: ZDHC (Roadmap to Zero); UNEP (Improving the transmission of information for POPs); GRI 303: Water and Efluents; GRI 306: Waste

questions.sdg_target: 3.c Support employee health capacity
questions.kpi: % annual budget allocated to employees receiving annual health check-ups
questions.question: To what extent does the company invest and sustain investment over time in occupational health services that reduce absenteeism and strengthen long-term workforce productivity?

awareness.text: Evaluate existing occupational health services (OHS) for both direct and contracted workers; assess absenteeism, ergonomic risks, and chronic-disease factors.
awareness.source: R171 - Occupational Health Services Recommendation, 1985 (No. 171); ISSA Guidelines on Workplace Health PromotionGRI 403: Occupational Health & Safety (2018)

developing.text: Establish formal OHS programs, including regular check-ups, screening, ergonomics assessments, and preventive interventions; track improvement in productivity metrics.
developing.source: Guidelines on occupational safety uidelines on occupational safety and health management systems nd health management systems ILO-OSH 2001; ISO 45001:2018 – Occupational Health & Safety Management; UN Global Compact (Occupational Safety and Health) & (Investing in Workplace Health and Well-being);

leading.text: Achieve universal OHS coverage; integrate health indicators into productivity dashboards; publicly report on health outcomes and ROI.
leading.source: ILO (Safety and Health at Work); ILO guide to International Labour Standards on Occupational Safety and Health; WHO (Occupational health); GRI 403: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY 2018

questions.sdg_target: 3.4 Promote employee well-being
questions.kpi: Access to mental health resources and flexible hours
questions.question: To what extent does the company provide, monitor and adapt access to mental health support services and flexible working arrangements in response to evolving employee needs?

awareness.text: Identify stressors and psychosocial risks; map availability of mental health services, workload practices, and work–life balance gaps.
awareness.source: WHO (Mental health at work); ILO (Mental health at work); GRI 401: Employment

developing.text: Introduce Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs), counseling services, burnout-prevention programs, and flexible work schemes (remote, flex-time, reduced hours).
developing.source: ILO (Workplace stress: A collective challenge); ILO ( Workplace stress: A collective challenge); WHO healthy workplace framework and model; UN Global Compact (Investing in Workplace Health and Well-being)

leading.text: Integrate mental health into HR strategy; report well-being KPIs (stress reduction, satisfaction, retention); evaluate managers on well-being leadership competencies.
leading.source: WHO (Global report on health equity for persons with disabilities); ILO (Guidance on Achieving Decent Work in Global Trade); GRI 403: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY 2018; GRI 401: Employment

questions.sdg_description: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all
questions.sdg_target: 4.6 Ensure inclusive access to education
questions.kpi: % of employees trained in textile recycling & upcycling techniques
questions.question: To what extent does the company provide and progressively expand employee training on textile recycling, upcycling, and circular design practices?

awareness.text: Assess current staff understanding of circularity and waste reduction; identify knowledge gaps in textile recycling, upcycling, and design for reuse.
awareness.source: EMF (The Circular Design for Fashion Book: A journey towards the future of design); ISO 59004:2024 Circular economy — Vocabulary, principles and guidance for implementation; UNESCO (2023) – Education for Sustainable Development Framework

developing.text: Create structured learning modules on circular textile systems; integrate life-cycle thinking, material selection, and waste prevention into technical and design roles.
developing.source: EMF (Resources for circular economy education and lifelong learning); GRI 301: Materials (2020); UN Global Compact (Accelerating a Sustainable Future)

leading.text: Establish accredited internal “Circular Skills” programs; share outcomes (trained staff, design improvements, waste reduction) in sustainability reporting.
leading.source: ISO 59020:2024 Circular economy — Measuring and assessing circularity performance; EMF (Circular economy in practice: Case studies and company examples); GRI 404: Training and Education (2016)

questions.sdg_description: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all
questions.sdg_target: 4.7 Sustainability education
questions.kpi: Inclusion of sustainability in worker orientation programs
questions.question: To what extent has the company integrated and updated continuous environmental and sustainability training into employee onboarding and learning programs over time

awareness.text: Identify sustainability-related training gaps; include core topics like energy, water, waste, and chemicals management in onboarding.
awareness.source: UNESCO 2020 (Education for sustainable development: a roadmap); ISO 14001:2015 Environmental management systems — Requirements with guidance for use; UN Global Compact (The Academy The online learning platform of the UN Global Compact)

developing.text: Embed sustainability learning in all job functions and performance reviews; track participation and effectiveness of training modules.
developing.source: GRI 404: Training and Education (2016); ISO 14031:2021 Environmental management — Environmental performance evaluation — Guidelines; UNEP (Greening the Blue Report 2023)

leading.text: Offer accredited sustainability certifications or micro-credentials; publicly report employee-training hours and outcomes in ESG reports.
leading.source: UNESCO (SDGs and Greening TVET); UN Global Compact (2023) – SDG Ambition Accelerator; GRI 2: General Disclosures 2021; GRI 404: TRAINING AND EDUCATION 2016

questions.sdg_description: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all
questions.sdg_target: 4.4 Promote skills for work
questions.kpi: % of annual budget for employees to enrolled in job-relevant upskilling or certification
questions.question: To what extent does the company support employees in acquiring new skills or certifications that enhance both individual career prospects and company competitiveness?

awareness.text: Conduct a workforce-skills gap assessment; identify critical technical, digital, and green skills relevant to current and future business competitiveness.
awareness.source: ILO (Skills for green jobs); OECD Skills Outlook 2023

developing.text: Fund continuous-learning and certification opportunities (e.g., digital, sustainability, eco-design); establish mentoring or apprenticeship programs.
developing.source: GRI 404: Training and Education (2016); ILO (Skills for green jobs); OECD (Greener Skills and Jobs)

leading.text: Link upskilling programs with innovation outcomes and performance incentives; report % of employees trained and business impact metrics.
leading.source: ILO (oward lifelong skills development for decent work); UN Global Compact (2023) – CFO Principles on Skills Investment; GRI 404: TRAINING AND EDUCATION 2016; GRI 203: Indirect Economic Impacts 2016

questions.sdg_description: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all
questions.sdg_target: 4.5 Empower marginalized employees
questions.kpi: Number of marginalized or underrepresented employees receiving training
questions.question: Does the company provide provide and expand targeted skill development opportunities for underrepresented or marginalized groups, and track participation relative to workforce composition over time?

awareness.text: Assess representation gaps (gender, youth, disability, migrant status) in training and promotion; set inclusion objectives in HR and CSR policies.
awareness.source: ILO online resources on Gender; UN Women (Women's Empowerment Principles); GRI 405: Diversity and Equal Opportunity (2016)

developing.text: Create targeted education programs for marginalized groups (e.g., women in technical roles, youth apprenticeships, training for persons with disabilities).
developing.source: ILO (Skills Development and Lifelong Learning: Resource Guide for Workers’ Organizations); ILO Skills Development andLifelong Learning Resource Guide for Workers’ Organizations); UN Women (Economic empowerment); GRI 404: TRAINING AND EDUCATION 2016; GRI 405: DIVERSITY AND EQUAL OPPORTUNITY 2016

leading.text: Track and publicly disclose participation and promotion rates for marginalized employees; partner with NGOs and education providers to scale inclusion programs.
leading.source: ILO (Disability and work); UN Women (Women's Empowerment Principles)GRI 405: DIVERSITY AND EQUAL OPPORTUNITY 2016

questions.sdg_target: 5.5 Promote women's leadership & entrepreneurship
questions.kpi: Percentage of women employed in textile recycling/upcycling processes
questions.question: To what extent are women equally and increasingly represented over time, in decision-making and participation in the company’s circular initiatives?

awareness.text: Map women’s representation in all circular initiatives (eco-design, recycling, take-back, circular business models, innovation teams) and compare with overall workforce and leadership composition. Integrate gender equality into your circular strategy (targets, roles, KPIs).
awareness.source: UN Women & UN Global Compact – Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs):; GRI 405: Diversity and Equal Opportunity 2016;

developing.text: Set minimum gender-balance objectives for circular taskforces and steering groups; establish leadership and technical training pathways for women in circular design, recycling, and innovation roles; track promotion rates of women into circular-economy positions.
developing.source: UN Women 2011 (Women’s Empowerment Principles: Equality Means Business); UN Global Compact – Endorse the Women’s Empowerment Principles; Ellen MacArthur Foundation – The Circular Economy (overview)

leading.text: Formally commit (e.g. WEPs signatory) to gender-balanced governance of circular initiatives; disclose gender-disaggregated data on participation and leadership in circular projects and set public targets for women’s leadership across the circular value chain.
leading.source: UN Women (Women’s Empowerment Principles: A snapshot of 350 companies in the G7); ILO Action Plan for Gender Equality 2022–25; GRI 405: DIVERSITY AND EQUAL OPPORTUNITY 2016

questions.sdg_target: 5.5 Ensure equal workplace safety
questions.kpi: Implementation of gender-inclusive workplace safety measures
questions.question: Has the company assessed and regularly updated and addressed gender-specific risks in workplace health & safety policies (e.g., ergonomic design of equipment, protective gear fit)?

awareness.text: Review OSH policies and risk assessments for gender bias (PPE fit, ergonomic design, exposure types, shift patterns, reproductive health risks). Collect sex-disaggregated injury, illness, and near-miss data.
awareness.source: ILO (Gender and Occupational Safety and Health); ILO (10 Keys for gender sensitive OSH practice – Guidelines for gender mainstreaming in occupational safety and health); WHO (WHO healthy workplace framework and model)

developing.text: Adapt OSH measures to gender-specific needs (PPE sizing, workstation design, lifting and repetitive-task limits, pregnancy/breastfeeding protections); ensure women’s participation in OSH committees and incident investigations.
developing.source: ILO (Gender and its Relationship to Occupational Safety and Health); ILO (More protection, less inequality: The urgent need for a gender perspective in occupational safety and health); Healthy workplaces: a model for action

leading.text: Mainstream gender into OSH management systems and audits; publish gender-disaggregated OSH indicators and case studies of risk reduction; align with ILO guidance and WHO healthy-workplace principles.
leading.source: ILO (10 Keys for Gender Sensitive OSH Practice); WHO (Healthy workplace); GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety 2018

questions.sdg_target: 5.4 Recognize and value unpaid care and domestic work
questions.kpi: Percentage of women in the workforce benefiting from paid family leave and childcare support
questions.question: To what extent does the company ensure and expand access to paid family leave, childcare facilities, or flexible work arrangements for women employees?

awareness.text: Map current policies on parental leave, family leave, flexible working, and childcare support; compare against ILO standards and identify gender gaps in uptake and career progression.
awareness.source: C156 - Workers with Family Responsibilities Convention, 1981 (No. 156); UN Women (Women's Empowerment Principles); ILO – Gender equality

developing.text: Introduce or enhance paid parental leave (for all genders), family-care leave, flexible hours/remote work, and childcare support (on-site facilities, subsidies or partnerships). Track usage by gender and contract type.
developing.source: GRI 401: Employment 2016 – includes Disclosure 401-3 on parental leave; WEPs Gender Gap Analysis Tool; REGULATORY IMPACT ASSESSMENT OF C156 – WORKERS WITH FAMILY RESPONSIBILITIES CONVENTION

leading.text: Align company policy with ILO C156 principles; ensure equal access to flexible work and leave for all genders; report on family-friendly benefits and their impact on retention, promotion, and pay equity.
leading.source: ILO (Workers with Family Responsibilities Convention, 1981 (No. 156)); GRI 401: Employment 2016

questions.sdg_target: 5.2 Eliminate violence and harassment against women
questions.kpi: Policies and mechanisms to prevent workplace harassment
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, regularly reviewed and strengthened anti-harassment and discrimination policies supported by confidential reporting mechanisms?

awareness.text: Review existing codes of conduct, grievance mechanisms, and HR policies against ILO C190 benchmarks; identify whether gender-based violence and harassment are explicitly covered and understood by workers.
awareness.source: ILO (Violence and harassment in the world of work); C190 - Violence and Harassment Convention, 2019 (No. 190); GRI 406: Non-discrimination 2016

developing.text: Adopt and communicate a zero-tolerance policy for violence, harassment, and discrimination; create multiple confidential reporting channels (hotlines, ombudsperson, digital tools); ensure protection from retaliation and clear investigation procedures.
developing.source: ILO – C190 Guide: Ending violence and harassment in the world of work; ITUC / ILO partners – ILO Convention 190: Towards a world of work free from violence and harassment; UN Women (Women's Empowerment Principles)

leading.text: Integrate C190 principles into enterprise agreements and supplier codes; train all managers and workers regularly; publish data on incidents and corrective actions (in line with GRI 406-1) while safeguarding confidentiality; involve women workers and unions in design and review of policies.
leading.source: Eliminating Violence and Harassment in the World of Work Convention No. 190, Recommendation No. 206, and the accompanying Resolution; GRI 406: Non-discrimination 2016 (incl. Disclosure 406-1 on incidents); UN Women (Women’s Empowerment Principles: A snapshot of 350 companies in the G7)

questions.sdg_target: 6.4 Improve water efficiency
questions.kpi: % of reused water in production or industrial processes
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, expanded or improved measures (e.g., water-saving technologies, closed-loop dyeing) to increase water-use efficiency in production?

awareness.text: Map water use across processes (spinning, dyeing, finishing, washing); quantify baseline withdrawals, consumption, and discharge; identify hotspots where closed-loop or low-liquor technologies could be introduced.
awareness.source: ISO 46001:2019 Water efficiency management systems — Requirements with guidance for use; ISO 14046:2014; Environmental management — Water footprint — Principles, requirements and guidelines; GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018

developing.text: Introduce water-efficient machinery (low-liquor dyeing, counter-current rinsing, condensate reuse) and internal re-use loops for suitable streams; embed water efficiency objectives and monitoring in a formal management system.
developing.source: ISO 46001: Water Efficiency Management Systems (WEMS) Certification; UN Global Compact – CEO Water Mandate (corporate water stewardship); CEO Water Mandate – Corporate Water Disclosure Guidelines

leading.text: Certify a water-efficiency management system (e.g., ISO 46001), integrate water-footprint results into design and process choices, and disclose water efficiency KPIs (litres/kg textile, % water reused) in sustainability reports.
leading.source: ISO 46001:2019 Water efficiency management systems — Requirements with guidance for use; ISO 14046:2014 Environmental management — Water footprint — Principles, requirements and guidelines; GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018

questions.sdg_target: 6.4 Increase water-use efficiency
questions.kpi: Percentage of wastewater treated before discharge
questions.question: Has the company installed operated, and continuously improved wastewater treatment systems (e.g., filtration, biological treatment) to reduce pollution and ensure compliance with discharge standards?

awareness.text: Identify all wastewater streams (process, cooling, sanitary); characterize key pollutants (colour, COD/BOD, salts, chemicals) and applicable regulatory or buyer requirements; map current treatment capacity and gaps.
awareness.source: GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018; UNEP (Technical guidelines); UNEP 2024 (Guidance on wastewater and solid waste management for manufacturing of antibiotics);

developing.text: Install and operate appropriate treatment (screening, equalization, biological treatment, filtration, sludge handling); monitor effluent quality (pH, COD/BOD, TSS, key chemicals) and maintain records to demonstrate compliance and continual improvement.
developing.source: UNEP (GREEN INFRASTRUCTURE GUIDE FOR WATER MANAGEMENT); GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018; ISO 14046:2014 Environmental management — Water footprint — Principles, requirements and guidelines

leading.text: Align treatment with best available techniques; explore water reclamation for process reuse; conduct water-footprint assessments for products and sites, and publicly disclose performance through CEO Water Mandate or similar platforms.
leading.source: CEO Water Mandate – Corporate Water Disclosure; UN Global Compact – Water: Essential for life, critical for business; ISO 14046:2014 Environmental management — Water footprint — Principles, requirements and guidelines

questions.sdg_target: 6.4 Improve water efficiency
questions.kpi: % reduction in water treatment costs through process efficiency
questions.question: To what extent has the company improved water and wastewater management efficiency to reduce operational costs and strengthen long-term financial sustainability?

awareness.text: Quantify the full cost of water (abstraction, treatment, energy for pumping/heating, chemicals, discharge fees) and link it to production volumes; identify cost-saving opportunities from efficiency and reuse.
awareness.source: ISO 46001:2019 Water efficiency management systems — Requirements with guidance for use; ISO 14046:2014 Environmental management — Water footprint — Principles, requirements and guidelines; UN Global Compact (Determine your path to water stewardship)

developing.text: Integrate water-efficiency targets into financial planning and capital budgeting (e.g., ROI for water-saving equipment, payback on reuse systems); monitor reduction in water and wastewater costs as part of resource-efficiency KPIs.
developing.source: CEO Water Mandate – Corporate Water Disclosure Guidelines; UN Global Compact (Determine your path to water stewardship); GRI 201: Economic Performance 2016

leading.text: Use standardized water-efficiency and water-footprint approaches to support scenario analysis (e.g., rising tariffs, scarcity risk); disclose cost savings and risk-reduction benefits of water projects, and reinvest part of savings in further efficiency or community WASH.
leading.source: UN Global Compact (Water: Essential for Life, Critical for Business — Why Companies Must Act Now); ISO 46001:2019 Water efficiency management systems — Requirements with guidance for use; A practical guide for SMEs: ISO 14046 Water footprint

questions.sdg_target: 6.2 Ensure adequate sanitation & hygiene for community
questions.kpi: Percentage of workers with access to safe sanitation & hygiene facilities
questions.question: Has the company ensured and maintained universal access to clean drinking water, safe sanitation, and hygiene facilities over time?

awareness.text: Assess WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene) conditions at all sites (including supplier facilities where possible): availability, quality, privacy, gender-appropriateness, and accessibility of drinking water, toilets, and handwashing stations.
awareness.source: WHO (Water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH)); UNICEF (Water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH)); ILO / WHO / UNICEF – WASH@Work: A Self-Training Handbook

developing.text: Implement company standards for WASH provision (minimum ratios of toilets to workers, separate facilities for women and men, menstrual-hygiene facilities, safe drinking water, handwashing with soap); train supervisors and workers on hygiene practices and monitor compliance.
developing.source: CEO Water Mandate (WASH4Work: Baseline and Monitoring Indicators (2021)); WASH4Work – tools & resources for workplace WASH; UNICEF (HAND HYGIENE FOR ALL: SUMMARY OF RESOURCE GUIDE FOR BUSINESS)

leading.text: Commit publicly to universal, gender-responsive WASH for all workers across operations and priority suppliers; integrate WASH indicators into social audits and ESG reporting, and partner with local stakeholders to extend WASH access to surrounding communities.
leading.source: CEO Water Mandate (WASH4Work Insights Report (2022); ILO / WHO / UNICEF – WASH@Work: A Self-Training Handbook

questions.sdg_target: 7.3 Improve energy efficiency
questions.kpi: Reductions in energy requirements of sold products and services
questions.question: To what extent does the company recover and reuse energy within its textile production cycle and increase recovered energy relative to a defined baseline year?

awareness.text: Identify where energy is lost (e.g., heat from dyeing/finishing machines, steam systems, compressed air leaks, exhaust air); assess technical feasibility of heat recovery and internal reuse loops.
awareness.source: UNIDO (Energy Efficiency in Industry); ISO 50001:2018 Energy management systems ; GRI 302: Energy 2016

developing.text: Install heat-recovery systems (e.g., dyeing-machine heat exchangers, boiler economizers), reuse condensate in pre-heating, and integrate thermal-loop monitoring into an energy-management system.
developing.source: UNEP-Energy; ISO 50001 Energy Management System; IEA (ndustry – Energy Efficiency Policy Toolkit 2025 – Analysis)

leading.text: Set circular energy targets (% recovered energy), link them to ISO 50001 certification, and publicly disclose energy-recovery performance and reductions in primary energy demand.
leading.source: ISO 50001 – Energy Management Systems; UN Global Compact (Taking climate action is good for business); GRI 302: Energy 2016

questions.sdg_target: 7.2 Increase the share of renewable energy
questions.kpi: % of energy from renewable sources
questions.question: To what extent has the company replaced fossil-based energy with renewable sources and increased the renewable share over time?

awareness.text: Quantify current energy mix (grid electricity, fuels, heat, steam) and identify hotspots for renewable-energy substitution; analyze regulatory/market incentives or PPAs (power purchase agreements).
awareness.source: UNEP- Energy; IEA – Renewables 2023/2024; GRI 302: Energy

developing.text: Implement renewable-energy procurement (PPAs, green tariffs), install on-site solar/biomass/biogas heat systems, and replace fossil fuels in boilers where possible.
developing.source: UN Global Compact – Business Ambition for 1.5 °C; RE100 (corporate 100% renewable initiative); IEA website Advancing Decarbonisation through Clean Electricity Procurement

leading.text: Commit to science-based decarbonization targets; achieve majority-renewable electricity or heat; certify renewable sourcing and publicly disclose progress annually.
leading.source: Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi); UNEP (Renewable Energy); GRI 302: Energy

questions.sdg_target: 7.3 Improve energy efficiency
questions.kpi: Investment in energy-efficient production technologies
questions.question: To what extent has the company invested over time in upgrading machinery, equipment, or processes to improve energy efficiency and reduce production costs?

awareness.text: Conduct an energy audit to identify outdated or inefficient machinery (motors, boilers, compressors, dyeing machines) and evaluate the financial impact of energy inefficiency (fuel, electricity, downtime costs).
awareness.source: ISO 50002-1:2025 Energy audits; GRI 201: Economic Performance; IEA (Energy Management for Industry)

developing.text: Invest in high-efficiency motors, variable-frequency drives, optimized boilers, LED lighting, and smart automation; include energy criteria in procurement; track ROI on efficiency investments.
developing.source: UNIDO – Industrial Energy Efficiency Programme; ISO 50001 Energy Management System; IEA (Industry - Energy System)

leading.text: Integrate energy efficiency into core business strategy; report cost savings, avoided emissions, and productivity gains; require suppliers to adopt similar systems.
leading.source: UN Global Compact (Decent Work Toolkit for Sustainable Procurement); ISO 50001 – Energy Management Systems; GRI 302: Energy

questions.sdg_target: 7.3 Improve energy efficiency
questions.kpi: Employee training and awareness programs on energy efficiency
questions.question: Does the company provide provide regular and updated training and engagement programs on energy-saving practices, with participation and effectiveness tracked over time?

awareness.text: Assess current employee understanding of energy practices, identify high-impact behaviors (machine shutdown, leaks, temperature settings), and map training gaps across roles.
awareness.source: ILO – Skills for Green Jobs; GRI 404: Training and Education; UNEP- Energy

developing.text: Develop structured employee training on efficient equipment operation, shutdown procedures, leak reporting, and renewable-energy use. Launch awareness campaigns and operator-level certifications.
developing.source: ILO – Skills for Green Jobs; UN Global Compact-Environment; GRI 404: Training and Education

leading.text: Establish a “Clean Energy Champions” program; incentive teams for energy-saving innovations; publicly disclose training hours and employee engagement outcomes tied to energy KPIs.
leading.source: ILO – Skills for Green Jobs; UN Global Compact-Environment; GRI 404: Training and Education; UNEP-Energy

questions.sdg_target: 8.3 Promote circular business models in textiles
questions.kpi: Percentage of textile production linked to circular business models
questions.question: To what extent has the company integrated and continuously assessed circular business models (e.g., clothing rental, resale, repair, take-back) into its operations to create new value and reduce textile waste?

awareness.text: Map current end-of-life pathways (landfill, recycling, reuse); assess feasibility of rental, resale, repair, upcycling, or take-back models; identify consumer demand and barriers.
awareness.source: Ellen MacArthur Foundation – Circular Economy in Fashion; UNEP (Finance and Economic Transformations); OECD (Extended producer responsibility in the garments sector)

developing.text: Pilot circular business models: in-store repair services, clothing rental programs, resale marketplaces, or take-back incentives; measure returns, customer engagement, and waste reduction.
developing.source: Ellen MacArthur Foundation – The Jeans Redesign; GRI 306: Waste 2020; UNEP (Circularity and Used Textile Trade Project)

leading.text: Scale circular business models across product categories; integrate reverse logistics; disclose circular revenue share and textile-waste prevention outcomes; collaborate with municipalities or NGOs on large-scale collection.
leading.source: EMF (Circular economy in practice: Case studies and company examples); ISO 59020:2024 Circular economy ; GRI 306: WASTE 2020

questions.kpi: Reduction of water & chemical usage per batch production

awareness.text: Evaluate production inefficiencies in energy use, water, chemicals, and waste; conduct an environmental performance assessment aligned with ISO and GRI frameworks.
awareness.source: ISO 14001:2015 Environmental management systems; UNEP (Finance and Economic Transformations); GRI 302 & 303 & 305 (energy, water, emissions)

developing.text: Introduce low-impact production technologies (e.g., digital printing, enzymatic processing, low-liquor dyeing, renewable heat systems), track reductions in energy, water, chemicals, and emissions.
developing.source: ISO 14031:2021 Environmental management; OECD (Achieving the Successful Transfer of Environmentally Sound Technologies); UNEP (Decoupling: natural resource use and environmental impacts from economic growth)

leading.text: Commit to science-based sustainability targets; integrate eco-efficiency into long-term planning; publicly report environmental improvements using globally recognized disclosure standards.
leading.source: Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi); UN Global Compact (Caring for Climate); Waste (GRI 306); Emissions (GHG) (GRI 305); Water and Effluents (GRI 303); Energy (GRI 302)

questions.sdg_target: 8.2 Improve productivity through sustainable innovation
questions.kpi: Percentage of revenue from sustainable textile products
questions.question: To what extent has the company expanded its portfolio or revenue streams through sustainable textile products, and increased the share of sustainable revenue over time?

awareness.text: Analyze current product portfolio for sustainability performance; identify opportunities for bio-based fibers, recycled-content textiles, or low-impact material innovations.
awareness.source: OECD (Circular economy policies and country studies); EMF (Material selection); GRI 201: Economic Performance 2016

developing.text: Invest in R&D to develop low-impact, circular, or recyclable textile products; establish innovation partnerships (suppliers, research institutes, start-ups); track sales of sustainable products and associated savings.
developing.source: UN Global Compact (Your Tools to Advance the SDGs); ISO 56002:2019 Innovation management; OECD (Metrics for green innovation )

leading.text: Scale sustainable product lines; link performance metrics (e.g., % sustainable revenue) to corporate strategy; disclose innovation outcomes in ESG reporting.
leading.source: GRI 301: Materials; UN Global Compact – SDG Innovation Accelerator ; OECD Circular economy policies and country studies;

questions.sdg_target: 8.5 Promote equal pay & gender equality in textile workforce
questions.kpi: Gender pay gap reduction & women in leadership
questions.question: Has the company implemented and expanded over time programs to create employment opportunities, vocational training, or apprenticeships for young workers entering the textile industry?

awareness.text: Identify youth employment gaps, barriers to accessing textile jobs, and existing training programs; benchmark against ILO youth-employment guidelines.
awareness.source: ILO – Youth Employment Programme; ILO (Skills and lifelong learning); GRI 404: Training and Education

developing.text: Launch targeted apprenticeship, vocational training, and upskilling programs for young workers—including technical, digital, and green skills—while promoting pay equity and transparent career pathways.
developing.source: ILO – Skills for Green Jobs; UN Women (Women’s Empowerment Principles: Equality Means Business); OECD – Skills and the Future of Work

leading.text: Institutionalize youth employment pipelines, partner with technical schools, ensure equal pay and gender equality in training access, and publish gender- and age-disaggregated training/employment data.
leading.source: ILO-Youth employment; UN Global Compact – Decent Work Toolkit; GRI 405: Diversity & Equal Opportunity 2016

awareness.source: EMF-Circular economy in fashion; ISO 59004:2024 Circular economy; The UNEP Textile Initiative;

developing.text: Integrate circular design criteria into product development (design for longevity, disassembly, mono-materiality, recycled content); set measurable goals and update sourcing specifications and technical packs.
developing.source: EMF-Circular design: turning ambition into action; ISO 14006:2020 Environmental management systems; GRI 301: Materials

leading.text: Apply advanced circular-design frameworks across all collections; track circularity indicators (recycled content %, recyclability score, product-life extension metrics); publicly report progress.

awareness.source: ISO 14001:2015 Environmental management systems;UNEP-Finance and Economic Transformations; GRI 302/303/305 – Energy, Water, Emissions

developing.text: Upgrade machinery (low-liquor dyeing, digital printing, high-efficiency motors, solar thermal, modern boilers); integrate energy/water monitoring systems; optimize production layouts to reduce losses.
developing.source: UNIDO-Resource Efficient and Cleaner Production (RECP) |; ISO 50001:2018 Energy management systems; OECD-Green technology and innovation

developing.text: Fund R&D in sustainable fibers (recycled, bio-based), low-impact dyeing/finishing, digital manufacturing, and recycling technologies; establish partnerships with research institutes and startups.
developing.source: The UNEP Textile Initiative; EMF-Circular economy in fashion; GRI 201: Economic Performance 2016

questions.sdg_description: Build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and foster innovation
questions.sdg_target: 9.4 Upgrade infrastructure for skills
questions.kpi: % of staff involved in technical upskilling or equipment handling
questions.question: Does the company provide employees with continuous technical training and upskilling programs that enable effective use of new or upgraded production infrastructure?

awareness.text: Identify competency gaps linked to new infrastructure (automation, digital tools, upgraded machinery); assess training needs for technicians, operators, and maintenance staff.
awareness.source: ILO-Skills and lifelong learning; GRI 404: Training & Education; UNESCO-UNEVOC – TVET & Skills Development

developing.text: Provide structured training on advanced machinery, automation, digital tools, and sustainability-driven technologies; integrate safety, efficiency, and maintenance modules.
developing.source: ILO-Skills and lifelong learning; UN Global Compact Academy – Skills & Sustainability Modules; GRI 404: Training and Education 2016

leading.text: Create long-term career pathways linked to advanced infrastructure; certify operators; publish outcomes (training hours, productivity gains, reduced incidents); ensure equal access for women and young workers.

awareness.source: ILO-Promoting decent work for all; UN Global Compact-Decent Work Toolkit for Sustainable Procurement; GRI 405: Diversity & Equal Opportunity

developing.source: OECD-Towards more environmentally sustainable supply chains; UN Women & UNGC – Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs); ILO-Skills and lifelong learning

questions.sdg_description: Reduce inequality within and among countries

questions.kpi: % of sustainability initiatives in production/operation driven by employee-led teams
questions.question: Does the company continuously ensure that all employees, regardless of role or background, are equally involved in workplace sustainability initiatives?

awareness.text: Review how sustainability decisions are made and who participates; identify representation gaps (role, age, gender, ethnicity).
awareness.source: UN Global Compact -Caring for Climate; OECD-The OECD Reinforcing Democracy InitiativeGRI 403 & 405 (participation, diversity, worker engagement)

developing.text: Create diverse, cross-role sustainability committees; provide equal participation opportunities in environmental programs (recycling teams, energy champions, waste audits).
developing.source: UNEP-Policies; GRI 403/405; ILO-Workers’ organizations and development cooperation

leading.text: Institutionalize inclusive participation through transparent nomination processes and track representation in sustainability governance; disclose participation data.
leading.source: GRI 405 disclosures; Stakeholder participation - OECD - IOC Toolkit; UN Global Compact-Guide to Corporate Sustainability

questions.sdg_description: Reduce inequality within and among countries

awareness.source: ILO-Equal Pay - An introductory guide; OECD – Income Inequality; GRI 202: Market Presence 2016

developing.text: Establish transparent salary bands, standardized promotion criteria, and clear bonus policies; ensure equal pay reviews and corrective measures.
developing.source: Equal Pay International Coalition; UN Global Compact – Gender Equality; GRI 405: Diversity and Equal Opportunity; GRI 202 (General Disclosures)

leading.text: Publish pay-equity achievements; conduct independent audits; integrate equitable compensation into HR policies, board oversight, and supplier requirements.

awareness.text: Map textile waste streams across operations and retail; identify existing municipal, SME, and NGO partners involved in collection, sorting, and recycling; assess volumes and current end-of-life routes (landfill, incineration, export).
awareness.source: GRI 306: Waste 2020; UNEP-Advancing circularity for used textiles; UNEP – Sustainable and Circular Textiles

developing.text: Co-design take-back, reuse, and recycling schemes with municipalities, social enterprises, and SMEs (e.g., urban collection points, sorting hubs, repair/upcycling workshops). Track quantities collected, reused, and recycled, and integrate waste-prevention targets into company strategy.
developing.source: UNEP and UN-Habitat are calling for zero waste good practices in fashion and textiles; GRI 306: Waste 2020; UNEP-Zero Waste Day shines a light on fashion and textiles

leading.text: Scale city-level circular textile systems (e.g., regional hubs for collection and mechanical/chemical recycling), publish case studies with city or NGO partners, and disclose performance (tonnes diverted, % textile waste reused/recycled, local jobs created).

developing.text: Install and operate appropriate emission-control technologies (e.g., filters, scrubbers, low-NOx burners), shift to cleaner fuels, and enforce good maintenance practices; monitor stack and fugitive emissions and report internally.
developing.source: WHO global air quality guidelines; UNEP-Air Quality; GRI 305: Emissions 2016

leading.text: Align site emission-reduction plans with WHO guideline values and local urban air-quality strategies; publish emissions data (e.g., NOx, SO₂, PM) and engage with local authorities and communities on air-quality improvements.

questions.sdg_description: Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable
questions.sdg_target: 11.A – Support for positive economic, social and environmental links between urban, peri-urban and rural areas
questions.kpi: Number or percentage of collaborations with local micro-enterprises (e.g., tailoring, textile repair, upcycling) in urban areas

developing.text: Establish commercial or partnership contracts with local micro-enterprises for repair, alteration, remanufacturing, and upcycling; co-design business models (e.g., repair vouchers, branded upcycled capsules) and measure jobs created and local income generated.
developing.source: GRI 413: Local Communities 2016; GRI 203: Indirect Economic Impacts 2016; Towards Zero Waste in Fashion and Textiles

leading.text: Create structured support programmes (micro-finance access, technical training, equipment donations, joint branding) for urban micro-enterprises; report on urban–rural value-chain linkages (e.g., rural fiber, urban repair, reuse) and social outcomes.
leading.source: UN-Habitat-Rescuing SDG 11 for a Resilient Urban Planet; GRI 203 & 413; UNEP-Circular Solutions to Achieve Climate Targets in the Textile Sector

developing.text: Introduce or strengthen measures such as subsidized or healthy canteen meals, safe company transport or transport allowances, flexible hours/shift design, and—where relevant—support for safe and decent housing (dormitories standards, housing allowances, or partnerships).
developing.source: GRI 401; WHO-Healthy workplaces: a model for action; ILO – Decent Work Indicators

leading.text: Embed quality-of-life measures into corporate policy (e.g., minimum standards for canteens, transport safety, support for commuting and childcare); track and report their impact on retention, absenteeism, and employee satisfaction, and engage with city authorities on mobility and housing solutions.
