questions.sdg_target: 1.5 – Strengthen resilience of vulnerable groups
questions.kpi: Integration of reusable/recyclable packaging solutions that generate local employment
questions.question: To what extent has the company integrated reusable or recyclable packaging models that also create employment or income opportunities in local communities (e.g., collection, sorting, remanufacturing) and upgraded them over time?

awareness.text: Build awareness of the social benefits of reusable/recyclable packaging; collect data on packaging waste and local employment opportunities; identify community partnerships and value-chain gaps using GRI 306-3 and ISO 14001 references.
awareness.source: Ellen MacArthur Foundation, Reuse – rethinking packaging (2019), OECD (2022), Global Plastics Outlook: Economic Drivers, Environmental Impacts and Policy Options

developing.text: Formalize circular packaging programmes employing local workers in collection, sorting, and reuse; set measurable targets (e.g., tonnes reused, number of local jobs created); integrate monitoring using life-cycle and social indicators.
developing.source: European Commission (2020), Circular Economy Action Plan, Ellen MacArthur Foundation, Reusable packaging business models (2023), Laubinger, F., E. Lanzi and J. Chateau (2020), “Labour market consequences of a transition to a circular economy: A review paper”, OECD Environment Working Papers, No. 162

leading.text: Communicate results (jobs created, packaging reuse rates); collaborate with municipalities, NGOs, and SMEs; replicate community-based circular models regionally.
leading.source: Ellen MacArthur Foundation, Unlocking a reuse revolution: scaling returnable packaging (2023), Circularity Gap Report (2022)

questions.sdg_target: 1.5 – Strengthen resilience for vulnerable workers
questions.kpi: Climate resilience and occupational safety in facilities
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented and periodically reviewed and upgraded climate-resilience measures (e.g., ventilation, cooling, flood protection) and integrated them into its occupational health and safety procedures?

awareness.text: Build awareness of heat and climate risks to factory workers; perform vulnerability assessments using ILO and UNDRR frameworks.
awareness.source: ILO (2019), Working on a Warmer Planet: The Impact of Heat Stress on Labour Productivity; UNDRR Sendai Framework

developing.text: Integrate resilience actions into OHS policies: improve ventilation, provide shaded rest areas, hydration, and emergency protocols; set and monitor performance targets.
developing.source: ISO 45001 (Occupational Health and Safety)

leading.text: Publicly disclose climate-resilience measures and outcomes; collaborate with brands, unions, and local authorities to scale good practices.
leading.source: ILO (Just transition Policy Brief-Occupational safety and health in a just transition) (2023)

questions.sdg_target: 1.2 – Reduce poverty through fair wages and inclusive employment
questions.kpi: Fair wages and inclusive hiring practices
questions.question: To what extent has the company ensured that employees receive fair and decent wages relative to a baseline year, and implemented inclusive recruitment practices for individuals from economically disadvantaged backgrounds?

awareness.text: Map current wage levels and inclusion gaps; benchmark against local living-wage standards; raise awareness of inclusive hiring methods.
awareness.source: ILO (A methodology to estimate the needs of workers and their families for the purpose of wage setting, including living wages)

developing.text: Establish policies guaranteeing decent wages and inclusive recruitment; set measurable targets (e.g., % above minimum wage, % from disadvantaged backgrounds); implement audits and reporting.
developing.source: ILO (Global Employment Policy Review 2020 - Employment policies for inclusive structural transformation)

leading.text: Communicate progress in social-impact reporting; engage in sectoral collaborations to scale fair-wage and inclusive-employment models.
leading.source: European Commission (Research in Action: how to define, measure and communicate the societal impact of your work?) (2024); OECD (LIVING WAGES IN CONTEXT: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS FOR OECD COUNTRIES) (2023)

questions.sdg_target: 1.4 – Ensure access to financial services and social benefits
questions.kpi: Employee access to financial literacy or savings programs
questions.question: Does the company provide or facilitate access to financial literacy training, savings schemes, or similar programs on an ongoing basis that strengthen workers’ financial security?

awareness.text: Identify workers’ access gaps to banking, savings, and benefits; collect baseline data; reference financial inclusion standards.
awareness.source: World Bank Group (Financial Inclusion) (2025); OECD/INFE (2022) Toolkit for Measuring Financial Literacy & Financial Inclusion

developing.text: Formalize partnerships with financial institutions or NGOs; offer training and savings schemes; define participation and savings-growth targets; monitor impact.
developing.source: OECD (Policy handbook on financial education in the workplace) (2022);

leading.text: Communicate outcomes (training reach, improved savings, reduced debt); collaborate with governments and supply-chain partners to replicate inclusion programmes across regions
leading.source: ILO (Inclusive Finance for Workers) (2019)

questions.sdg_target: 2.4 – Ensure sustainable food production systems and implement resilient agricultural practices
questions.kpi: Share of bio-based packaging produced from agricultural or food-processing by-products
questions.question: To what extent does the company use and track over time renewable and secondary bio-based raw materials, such as agricultural residues, forestry by-products, algae, or other non-food biomass, in its packaging products to reduce competition with food resources and support sustainable material cycles?

awareness.text: Assess the origin and type of bio-based inputs used in packaging; distinguish between food-grade feedstocks and secondary biomass such as crop residues, forest by-products, or algae. Promote awareness of life-cycle impacts and competition with food systems using ISO 14040 and ISO 14044 (LCA)
awareness.source: ISO (2006), ISO 14040/14044: Life-Cycle Assessment

developing.text: Adopt procurement policies prioritizing renewable, non-food and residual biomass feedstocks; integrate traceability of bio-based inputs through ISO 22095 (Chain of Custody) and disclose renewable-material share under GRI 301-1 and 301-2. Collaborate with suppliers to assess feedstock sustainability using FAO’s Sustainability Assessment of Food and Agriculture Systems (SAFA) framework.
developing.source: ISO (2020), ISO 22095: Chain of Custody; GRI (2020), GRI 301: Materials; FAO (2014), SAFA Guidelines: Sustainability Assessment of Food and Agriculture Systems

leading.text: Invest in R&D for next-generation bio-materials derived from agricultural or forestry residues and industrial side streams. Publicly commit to sourcing only non-food, renewable, and regenerative feedstocks and report progress through transparent life-cycle indicators (ISO 14067, GRI 301).
leading.source: ISO (2018), ISO 14067: Carbon Footprint of Products; Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2021), Circular Design for Food; UNEP (2024) Global Bioeconomy Assessment

questions.sdg_target: 2.5 – Maintain genetic diversity of cultivated plants and farm systems
questions.kpi: Biodiversity-friendly sourcing of bio-based feedstocks
questions.question: To what extent does the company ensure over time that its bio-based materials originate from supply chains verified for biodiversity protection and sustainable land-use practices (e.g., certified regenerative, organic, or biodiversity-friendly sources)?

awareness.text: Identify all bio-based inputs in packaging and their geographic origin; assess exposure to biodiversity risks such as monoculture feedstocks or land-use change. Raise internal awareness using FAO’s State of the World’s Biodiversity for Food and Agriculture and ISO 14055 guidance on sustainable land management.
awareness.source: FAO (2019), State of the World’s Biodiversity for Food and Agriculture; ISO (2017), ISO 14055-1: Guidelines for Establishing Good Practices for Sustainable Land Management; UNEP (2022), Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework

developing.text: Source bio-based raw materials from certified sustainable systems (e.g., FSC, PEFC, organic, or regenerative agriculture). Include biodiversity protection clauses in supplier codes and verify compliance through ISO 19011-based audits. Report sourcing volumes and certification coverage under GRI 304 (Biodiversity).
developing.source: GRI (2016), GRI 304: Biodiversity; FSC (2021), Forest Stewardship Standard; ISO (2018), ISO 19011: Guidelines for Auditing Management Systems

leading.text: Collaborate with producers to restore ecosystems and maintain genetic diversity of feedstocks; invest in regenerative agriculture projects that enhance soil health, pollinator habitats, and seed diversity. Publish impact metrics (hectares restored, biodiversity indicators improved) and align targets with the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration.
leading.source: UNEP & FAO (2021), UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration Strategy; GRI (2016), GRI 304: Biodiversity; FAO (Regenerative Agriculture)

questions.sdg_target: 2.3 – Double the productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers
questions.kpi: Procurement share from small-scale bio-feedstock producers
questions.question: To what extent has the company increased procurement from small-scale or cooperative producers of bio-feedstock materials for its packaging, thereby enhancing their income and market access over time?

awareness.text: Map current suppliers of bio-based or agricultural feedstocks and identify opportunities to engage small-scale or cooperative producers. Raise awareness of inclusive sourcing models and decent-work principles following ILO Recommendation 204 on the transition from informal to formal economy.
awareness.source: ILO (2015), Recommendation 204: Transition from the Informal to the Formal Economy; UN (2012), Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights; GRI (2016), GRI 204: Procurement Practices

developing.text: Establish inclusive procurement criteria favoring cooperatives and smallholders certified under fair-trade or sustainable agriculture schemes (e.g., Fairtrade International, Rainforest Alliance). Monitor sourcing volumes and price premiums paid; disclose progress in supplier-development indicators under GRI 204-1.
developing.source: GRI (2016), GRI 204: Procurement Practices; FAO (2020) Enabling sustainable food systems; OECD (2016) OECD-FAO Guidance for Responsible Agricultural Supply Chains

leading.text: Co-create long-term partnerships with small-scale producers through capacity-building, microfinance, and technology transfer. Track income growth and productivity improvements, and report shared-value outcomes aligned with the UN Sustainable Food Systems Roadmap.
leading.source: FAO Achieving SDG 2 without breaching the 1.5 °C threshold: A global roadmap; ILO Decent Work in the Rural Economy Report; ECD (2021), Building more resilient and sustainable global value chains through responsible business conduct

questions.sdg_target: 2.1 – End hunger and ensure access to safe, nutritious food for all
questions.kpi: Employee access to affordable and nutritious meals
questions.question: To what extent does the company provide affordable and nutritious food options for employees (e.g., canteen meals, subsidised food programs) at the workplace?

awareness.text: Assess employee nutritional needs and local food security conditions; promote awareness of healthy, balanced diets and sustainable nutrition using WHO dietary guidelines and FAO’s Sustainable Diets Framework.
awareness.source: WHO (2020), Healthy Diet Fact Sheet; FAO (2019), Sustainable Healthy Diets: Guiding Principles; GRI (2018), GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety

developing.text: Introduce workplace programs providing nutritious meals, food vouchers, or partnerships with local suppliers of sustainable foods. Integrate nutrition awareness into occupational health and well-being policies and monitor participation rates.
developing.source: ILO (Food at Work); WHO (2021), Workplace Health Promotion Framework; GRI (2018), GRI 401: Employment and GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety

leading.text: Implement comprehensive corporate nutrition strategies addressing food access, affordability, and education; measure health outcomes and employee satisfaction; share results in sustainability reports aligned with SDG 2 and GRI 401/403 indicators.
leading.source: FAO (Healthy Food Environment Checklist 2022 report); GRI (2018), GRI 401: Employment and GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety

questions.sdg_target: 3.9 – Reduce exposure to hazardous materials and ensure safe reuse
questions.kpi: Health and safety assurance for reused or recycled packaging materials
questions.question: To what extent does the company ensure that reused or recycled materials incorporated in packaging are systematically tested or certified as safe for human health and environmental use (e.g., food contact, absence of hazardous residues)?

awareness.text: Identify where reused or recycled materials enter the company’s packaging system; raise awareness of potential health and environmental risks associated with contaminants in secondary materials. Map supplier practices using ISO 18602 and ISO 18604 standards, and promote understanding of safe recycling and reuse aligned with the Ellen MacArthur Foundation’s “Vision for a Circular Economy for Plastic Packaging.”
awareness.source: ISO (2013), ISO 18602: Packaging and the environment — Optimization of the packaging system; ISO (2013), ISO 18604: Packaging and the environment — Material recycling; Ellen Macarthur Foundation (Our vision for plastics in a circular economy) (2021)

developing.text: Establish procedures to test and certify reused or recycled materials before use in packaging (e.g., migration, heavy metals, and NIAS testing for food-contact applications). Require supplier declarations of conformity and integrate verification steps in procurement and design processes using ISO 18604 and UNEP chemical safety guidance. Disclose data through GRI 301 (Materials) and GRI 306 (Waste).
developing.source: GRI (2020), GRI 301: Materials and GRI 306: Waste; UNEP (2025), Global Framework on Chemicals

leading.text: Implement third-party verification of recycled content safety and establish transparent specifications for material reuse in packaging. Collaborate with recyclers and suppliers to develop closed-loop systems ensuring traceability and safety. Communicate testing results and improvement actions in sustainability reports aligned with GRI 301 and ISO 18604.
leading.source: ISO (2013), ISO 18604: Packaging and the environment — Material recycling; Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2021), Global Commitment Progress Report;

questions.sdg_target: 3.9 – Reduce exposure to harmful substances
questions.kpi: Phase-out of hazardous substances in production
questions.question: To what extent does the company identify, replace and continuously revise potentially hazardous substances (e.g., chemical additives, inks, PFAS, etc.) with safer alternatives?

awareness.text: Develop a chemical inventory and identify substances of concern across the packaging value chain (e.g., additives, inks, coatings). Align mapping with UNEP’s Global Framework on Chemicals and Ellen MacArthur Foundation’s commitment to eliminate hazardous substances from packaging systems.
awareness.source: UNEP (2023), Global Framework on Chemicals; Ellen Macarthur Foundation (Our vision for plastics in a circular economy); OECD (2022), Substitution and Alternatives Assessment Toolbox

developing.text: Create a restricted substances list aligned with international chemical safety standards; conduct safer alternatives assessments following OECD guidelines. Integrate chemical substitution into ISO 14001 environmental management systems and report progress through GRI 301 (Materials) and 306 (Waste).
developing.source: ISO (2015), ISO 14001: Environmental Management Systems; GRI (2020), GRI 301: Materials and GRI 306: Waste; OECD (2021) Guidance on Key Considerations for the Identification and Selection of Safer Chemical Alternatives

leading.text: Adopt a time-bound strategy to phase out persistent and toxic substances such as PFAS; verify safer alternatives through testing and life-cycle assessments. Partner with suppliers and industry coalitions to “design out” chemical hazards in alignment with circular economy principles.
leading.source: UNEP (2025), Global Framework on Chemicals; Ellen Macarthur Foundation (Our vision for plastics in a circular economy; Fraunhofer CCPE (Global Plastics Outlook: Policy Scenarios to 2060)

questions.sdg_target: 3.C – Strengthen health workforce capacity
questions.kpi: Investment in employee health and safety programs
questions.question: To what extent does the company allocate and review resources to provide regular health check-ups and occupational health services for employees as part of its long-term productivity strategy?

awareness.text: Raise awareness among management and workers of the benefits of occupational health services and preventive health surveillance. Conduct a baseline assessment of workforce health coverage and workplace safety conditions in line with ILO Convention 161 and Recommendation 171.
awareness.source: ILO (1985), Convention No. 161 — Occupational Health Services; ILO (1985), Recommendation No. 171 — Occupational Health Services; GRI (2018), GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety

developing.text: Allocate funding for periodic medical check-ups and targeted health promotion programs; apply the hierarchy of controls to minimize risks. Track absenteeism, incident rates, and health outcomes through an ISO 45001-aligned management system.
developing.source: ISO (2018), ISO 45001: Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems; WHO/ILO (2022), Occupational Health Services: A Model for Action; GRI (2018), GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety

leading.text: Integrate occupational health surveillance with ergonomic, psychosocial, and preventive health programs. Monitor productivity and wellbeing indicators, disclose performance publicly, and benchmark progress against international OHS standards.
leading.source: ILO (2022), Global Strategy on Occupational Safety and Health; ISO (2018), ISO 45001 and ISO 45003: Psychological Health and Safety; GRI (2018), GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety

questions.sdg_target: 3.4 – Promote mental health and well-being
questions.kpi: Access to mental health support and flexible work arrangements
questions.question: To what extent does the company provide, monitor and adapt access to mental health support services and flexible working arrangements in response to evolving employee needs?

awareness.text: Build understanding of mental health as an organizational responsibility; identify psychosocial risk factors such as workload, harassment, and poor work-life balance. Promote awareness using WHO and ILO mental health guidance.
awareness.source: WHO & ILO (2022), Mental Health at Work: Policy Brief; ISO (2021), ISO 45003: Psychological Health and Safety at Work; GRI (2018), GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety

developing.text: Implement psychosocial risk management under ISO 45003; provide confidential employee assistance programs (EAP) and train managers in supportive leadership. Introduce flexible working arrangements to support well-being and inclusion.
developing.source: WHO (2022), Guidelines on Mental Health at Work; ISO (2021), ISO 45003: Psychological Health and Safety at Work; ILO (2020), Managing Work-related Psychosocial Risks during the COVID-19 Crisis

leading.text: Integrate mental health support into company-wide OHS and HR policies; set measurable targets (e.g., service uptake, stress reduction, retention rates). Publicly report outcomes under GRI 403 and 401, and share best practices across the industry.
leading.source: WHO & ILO (2022), Mental Health at Work: Policy Brief; ISO (2021), ISO 45003: Psychological Health and Safety at Work; GRI (2018), GRI 401: Employment and GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety

questions.sdg_description: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all
questions.sdg_target: 4.6 – Literacy and skills (incl. adult learning)
questions.kpi: Share of employees trained on circular packaging practices (design for recyclability/reuse, safe use of recycled content, take-back operations)
questions.question: To what extent does the company provide and update structured training for employees on circular packaging practices (e.g., design for reuse/recyclability, operating reuse/return systems, etc.)?

awareness.text: Map roles that influence packaging across the value chain (design, procurement, operations, reverse logistics) and identify skill gaps in circular concepts (reuse models, design for recyclability, reverse flows). Build a training baseline aligned to circular economy principles and basic eco-design.
awareness.source: ISO 59004:2024, Circular economy; Ellen MacArthur Foundation, Circular Design Guide; ISO 14006:2020, Guidelines for incorporating ecodesign.

developing.text: Create role-specific curricula (e.g., designers on design-for-reuse/recyclability; operations on return/refill handling; procurement on circular specifications). Track participation and learning outcomes using GRI 404 disclosures; embed LCA basics for packaging choices.
developing.source: GRI 404: Training and Education 2016; ISO 14040/14044, Life-cycle assessment.

leading.text: Institutionalize circular training as a competency framework tied to job families and promotion; run hands-on design sprints using EMF methods; certify advanced roles (e.g., internal “circular packaging lead”) and publish outcomes (projects delivered, % portfolio redesigned).
leading.source: Ellen MacArthur Foundation, Circular Design Guide; ISO 59004:2024 (organizational actions for circular economy)

questions.sdg_description: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all
questions.sdg_target: 4.7 – Education for sustainable development
questions.kpi: Integration of sustainability content in onboarding and periodic training (resources, emissions, chemicals, waste)
questions.question: To what extent has the company integrated environmental sustainability education into employee onboarding and regular training programmes?

awareness.text: Adopt an ESD (Education for Sustainable Development) policy for all employees; include core topics in onboarding: resource efficiency, safe and sustainable chemicals, and waste minimization.
awareness.source: UNESCO, ESD for 2030 toolbox; UNEP, Global Framework on Chemicals

developing.text: Integrate periodic (e.g., annual) training modules with case-based scenarios relevant to operations; include supplier-facing staff. Track completion and skills-upgrading per GRI 404; connect content to EMS and eco-design processes.
developing.source: GRI 404: Training and Education; ISO 14006:2020

leading.text: Embed ESD across functions (design, procurement, maintenance) with competency assessments and continuous improvement; publish learning KPIs and link to operational metrics (waste reduction, safe-chemical substitution).
leading.source: UNESCO, ESD for 2030; UNEP, Resource Efficiency & Circular Economy Target Setting Guidance

questions.sdg_description: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all
questions.sdg_target: 4.4 – Skills for decent work
questions.kpi: Investment and participation in job-relevant upskilling/certification (QA, food-contact compliance, eco-design, LCA, digital skills)
questions.question: To what extent does the company invest in employee upskilling (e.g. eco-design, LCA, digital/automation skills) in a way that measurably improves operational performance, productivity, and competitiveness over time?

awareness.text: Assess current and future skill needs for green and digital transformation (eco-design, LCA, data/automation for material flows). Establish a baseline of training hours and coverage.
awareness.source: ILO, Skills for Green Jobs; GRI 404: Training and Education

developing.text: Fund structured upskilling programs (eco-design via ISO 14006, LCA per ISO 14040/14044; digital skills for take-back/return analytics). Tie learning to process KPIs (line efficiency, defect rates, material yield).
developing.source: ISO 14006 (eco-design), ISO 14040/14044 (LCA); ILO, Anticipating Skill Needs for Green Jobs

leading.text: Create accredited internal academies and recognized credentials; co-design curricula with unions/partners; publish ROI on training (productivity, waste reductions) under GRI 404-2.
leading.source: GRI 404: Training and Education 2016; ILO, Skills for Green Jobs

questions.sdg_description: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all
questions.sdg_target: 4.5 – Equal access to education and training
questions.kpi: Equitable access to training for underrepresented groups; targeted programs to close gaps
questions.question: To what extent does the company ensure and monitor equal access to skill development and training opportunities for marginalised or underrepresented employees?

awareness.text: Audit participation in training by gender, age, contract type, migration/disability status where lawful; identify barriers (shift patterns, language, accessibility).
awareness.source: GRI 405: Diversity & Equal Opportunity; GRI 406: Non-discrimination.

developing.text: Set targeted inclusion measures (paid time for training, accessible formats, language support, mentoring). Track completion and progression by cohort; disclose under GRI 404 and 405.
developing.source: GRI 404/405 standards; UNEP Global Framework on Chemicals

leading.text: Institutionalize equitable learning pathways (apprenticeships, career ladders) with measurable advancement and pay outcomes; co-create programs with worker reps/ERGs; publish gap-closure targets and progress.
leading.source: GRI 405: Diversity and Equal Opportunity 2016; ILO Skills for Green Jobs

questions.sdg_target: 5.5 – Ensure women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities
questions.kpi: Representation of women in circular design and innovation initiatives (e.g., eco-design, recyclability, material substitution)
questions.question: To what extent has the company established, maintained, and improved women’s participation and decision-making roles in circular packaging activities (eco-design, recyclability, material recovery, sustainability innovation)?

awareness.text: Assess gender balance in teams working on circular-packaging design, R&D, and operations. Build awareness of women’s contribution to circular innovation and sustainable value-chain management using gender-inclusive design principles.
awareness.source: UN Global Impact-Endorse the Women's Empowerment Principles; Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2021), Circular Economy and Inclusion; GRI 405 (2016)

developing.text: Set measurable gender-participation targets against baseline for circular-economy projects; ensure women’s representation in decision-making and technical training (eco-design, recycling systems). Monitor gender balance through GRI 405-1 and report progress annually.
developing.source: GRI 405; ILO (2015), Gender equality and green jobs; Ellen MacArthur Foundation -The Global Commitment 2022

leading.text: Establish mentorship and leadership programs for women in circular innovation roles; integrate gender-responsive design into R&D processes; showcase female-led sustainability solutions publicly.
leading.source: GRI 405 (2016); UN Women's Strategic Plan 2022-2025; Ellen MacArthur Foundation A global roadmap for an inclusive circular economy (2023)&"Building Prosperity: Connecting Cities and Nature" (2024)

questions.sdg_target: 5.5 – Ensure equal workplace safety
questions.kpi: Gender-inclusive health and safety practices in production and chemical handling
questions.question: To what extent has the company identified, integrated and monitored gender-specific perspectives into its environmental management practices (involving women in environmental monitoring, resource efficiency initiatives, or sustainability committees)?

awareness.text: Assess gender-specific risks and participation levels in environmental programs and safety monitoring; build awareness on differentiated exposure to chemicals, waste, and ergonomics.
awareness.source: ILO Gender and Occupational Safety and Health; UNEP-Global Gender and Environment Outlook; ISO 14001

developing.text: Integrate gender considerations into environmental-management systems (ISO 14001 and ISO 45001); ensure women’s representation in sustainability and resource-efficiency committees; provide training on gender-responsive risk assessment.
developing.source: ISO 45003:2021; UN Women (2020), "Gender, Climate & Security: Sustaining inclusive peace on the frontlines of change"; GRI 403 (2018), Occupational Health and Safety

leading.text: Adopt a gender-responsive EMS auditing process (ISO 19011); collect sex-disaggregated data on environmental exposures and decisions; communicate outcomes through sustainability reporting and continuous-improvement plans.
leading.source: UN Women-Gender in Climate Policies Toolkit; ISO 14001 / ISO 19011; GRI 403 and 405 (2018/2016)

questions.sdg_target: 5.4 – Recognize and value unpaid care and domestic work
questions.kpi: Work-life balance and family support measures (paid leave, childcare, flexibility)
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, monitored, and improved access to paid family leave, childcare support, and flexible work arrangements for employees with care responsibilities?

awareness.text: Assess employee needs regarding childcare, eldercare, and work-life balance; communicate the social and economic benefits of family-friendly policies aligned with ILO Convention 156 on Workers with Family Responsibilities.
awareness.source: ILO (1981), Convention No. 156 – Workers with Family Responsibilities; ILO (2018), Care Work and Care Jobs for the Future of Decent Work; GRI 401: Employment 2016

developing.text: Implement and track over time paid parental leave, childcare subsidies, and flexible or remote-work options; monitor participation and satisfaction through HR metrics disclosed in GRI 401-2 (benefits) and GRI 405-2 (pay equality).
developing.source: GRI 401-2 (Employee benefits); UN Global Compact (2022), Target Gender Equality; ILO (2020) "Family-friendly policies and other good workplace practices in the context of COVID-19: Key steps for employers"

leading.text: Institutionalize a comprehensive “care-responsibility” framework combining parental leave, eldercare, and flexible arrangements; evaluate outcomes on retention, productivity, and gender balance; publicly disclose policies and results.
leading.source: ILO (2022), Care at Work: Investing in Care Leave and Services for a More Gender-Equal World of Work; UN Women (2022) "Gender-Responsive Business Guideline"; GRI 401 & 405

questions.sdg_target: 5.2 – Eliminate violence and harassment in the workplace
questions.kpi: Anti-harassment and non-discrimination policies with reporting mechanisms
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, monitored and improved anti-harassment and non-discrimination policies supported by confidential reporting and follow-up mechanisms?

awareness.text: Adopt a zero-tolerance policy on violence and harassment referencing ILO Convention 190; train managers and employees on recognizing and preventing misconduct; communicate available reporting channels.
awareness.source: ILO (2019), Convention No. 190 –Violence and harassment in the world of work; UN Women (2020), Safe and Fair ; GRI 406 (2016)

developing.text: Establish confidential reporting mechanisms; provide training for grievance officers; monitor case resolution and follow-up actions; disclose system coverage under GRI 406-1 (incidents of discrimination).
developing.source: GRI 406-1; ILO (2021) report on implementing Convention 190; UN Global Compact, Principle 6: Eliminate Discrimination in Employment

leading.text: Integrate anti-harassment measures into enterprise risk and OHS systems; conduct independent audits of policy effectiveness; publish aggregated data and continuous-improvement actions in sustainability reports.
leading.source: ILO Violence and Harassment in the World of Work report; ISO 45003 (2021), Psychological Health and Safety at Work; GRI 406 (2016), Non-discrimination

questions.sdg_target: 6.4 – Substantially increase water-use efficiency across all sectors
questions.kpi: Water reuse and recycling within operations
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, expanded and monitored closed-loop or water-recycling systems that allow treated process water to be reused in bio-based packaging production or other industrial operations?

awareness.text: Assess water inputs and discharge points across packaging production; identify opportunities for reuse and closed-loop treatment systems. Build awareness of circular-water principles using ISO 46001 and EMF’s industrial water-loop case studies.
awareness.source: ISO 46001 (2019), Water Efficiency Management Systems; Arup and the Ellen Macarthur Foundation’s latest report “From principles to practices: Realising the value of circular economy in real estate” (2022); UN Water -Summary progress update 2021 : SDG 6 – water and sanitation for all

developing.text: Install water-reuse technologies (filtration, ultrafiltration, RO, condensate recovery); monitor reuse ratios and water savings comparing to baseline values. Integrate targets into environmental management under ISO 14001 and disclose progress via GRI 303-3 (water recycled and reused).
developing.source: ISO 14001:2015 - Environmental management systems; GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018; OECD Work on Water

leading.text: Achieve closed-loop operation for process water; use treated effluents in non-critical production or utilities; publish verified water-recycling performance and innovation results aligned with ISO 46001 and EMF circular-design benchmarks.
leading.source: ISO 46001 (2019), Water Efficiency Management Systems; Ellen MacArthur Foundation-Circular Economy; UN Water-Blueprint for Acceleration: SDG 6 Synthesis Report on Water and Sanitation

questions.sdg_target: 6.3 – Improve water quality by reducing pollution
questions.kpi: Reduction of wastewater contamination from production
questions.question: To what extent has the company adopted, upgraded, and monitored cleaner production and wastewater-treatment measures to reduce pollutant loads and improve discharge quality?

awareness.text: Map all effluent streams; identify priority pollutants (e.g., inks, coatings, solvents). Build awareness of cleaner-production principles and compliance obligations using UNEP and ISO 14001 frameworks.
awareness.source: ISO 14001 (2015); GRI 303 (2018); UNEP (2023), Global Framework on Chemicals and Pollution Management

developing.text: Introduce cleaner-production technologies (low-VOC inks, water-based coatings); implement in-plant treatment and monitoring; report pollutant reduction under GRI 303-4 and 303-5. Conduct regular compliance audits per ISO 19011.
developing.source: GRI 303-4/303-5; ISO 19011 (2018); UNIDO Resource Efficient and Cleaner Production (RECP)

leading.text: Achieve near-zero liquid discharge or equivalent high-reuse performance; publish water-quality indicators (COD, BOD, heavy metals); partner with suppliers to extend cleaner-production standards throughout the value chain.
leading.source: ISO 14046 (2014); GRI 303 (2018); One Planet Network-Global Strategy for Sustainable Consumption and Production (SCP) 2023-2030

questions.sdg_target: 6.4 – Increase water-use efficiency
questions.kpi: Cost savings through water-efficiency optimization
questions.question: To what extent has the company integrated, monitored and improved water-efficiency or reuse measures as part of its cost-optimization and resource management strategy?

awareness.text: Quantify water consumption costs across facilities; link water-use data to operational expenses. Communicate the financial benefits of efficiency improvements using UN Water and ISO 46001 guidance.
awareness.source: ISO 46001 (2019); Summary Progress Update 2021: SDG 6 — water and sanitation for all; OECD (2021) Putting finance to work for a net zero, resilient, water secure future

developing.text: Integrate water-efficiency targets over multiple years into cost-optimization programs; invest in reuse infrastructure; measure payback periods and cost savings. Disclose results in GRI 303 and economic performance sections (GRI 201).

leading.text: Embed water-efficiency metrics in enterprise resource planning (ERP) and ESG dashboards; monetize water savings in sustainability reporting; reinvest savings into further innovation (e.g., smart sensors, AI monitoring).
leading.source: ISO 46001 (2019); WBCSD (2022), Business Guide to Water Valuation; UN Global Compact (2023), CEO Water Mandate Corporate Water Disclosure Guidelines

questions.sdg_target: 6.2 – Ensure access to safe drinking water and sanitation for all
questions.kpi: Workers’ access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH)
questions.question: To what extent has the company ensured, maintained, and periodically reviewed adequate sanitation and hygiene conditions for its workers, and contributed to improving such access for nearby communities?

awareness.text: Assess water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) facilities at all sites; raise awareness of workplace hygiene and its health impacts using WHO/UNICEF WASH guidance.
awareness.source: WHO & UNICEF Hand Hygiene for all : Resource Guide for Businesses; GRI 403 (2018); "Guidelines on occupational safety and health management systems, ILO-OSH 2001"

developing.text: Install safe-drinking-water dispensers and gender-segregated sanitation facilities; provide menstrual-hygiene products and awareness training; verify compliance with WHO water-quality standards and national OHS regulations.
developing.source: GRI 403-6 (2018); WHO (2020), Drinking-Water Quality Guidelines; ILO (2022) "Support Kit for Developing Occupational Safety and Health Legislation"

leading.text: Integrate WASH access into corporate-health and wellbeing programs; audit regularly with third-party verification; disclose coverage and improvement actions in sustainability reports and align with SDG 6.2 indicators.
leading.source: GRI 403 (2018); WHO & UNICEF Hand Hygiene for all : Resource Guide for Businesses; WASH4Work- WASH Pledge:Guiding principles A business commitment to WASH

questions.sdg_target: 7.3 – Improve energy efficiency
questions.kpi: Energy recovery and reuse within operations
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, expanded and monitored systems to recover and reuse waste heat or other forms of process energy within packaging production, thereby reducing overall energy demand?

awareness.text: Map energy flows across production lines to identify waste-heat sources and recovery potential. Build awareness of industrial-symbiosis and energy-loop concepts using ISO 50001 and circular-manufacturing guidance from the Ellen MacArthur Foundation.
awareness.source: ISO 50001 (2018); Ellen MacArthur Foundation-Universal circular economy policy goals (2021); GEO-6 | Global Environment Outlook (GEO) - UNEP

developing.text: Install waste-heat recovery (WHR) systems, regenerative burners, or heat-exchanger networks; monitor energy savings and CO₂ reductions against baseline values. Integrate recovery KPIs within ISO 50001 management reviews and disclose energy-reuse rates in GRI 302-3.
developing.source: GRI 302 (2016); ISO 50015 (2014); IEA "The Future of Heat Pumps" (2022)

leading.text: Implement fully closed-loop thermal-energy systems or industrial-symbiosis exchanges with nearby facilities; use recovered energy to power ancillary processes. Publicly report avoided-energy consumption and emission savings.
leading.source: ISO 50001 & ISO 50047 (2016); Ellen MacArthur Foundation-"The Global Commitment 2023 Progress Report,"; UNIDO Industrial Decarbonization

questions.sdg_target: 7.2 – Increase the share of renewable energy
questions.kpi: Renewable energy sourcing and strategy
questions.question: To what extent has the company developed, implemented, and progressed a strategy to replace fossil-based energy with renewable sources across its operations?

awareness.text: Quantify total energy mix and emissions baseline; raise awareness of renewable-energy options and certification schemes (e.g., I-REC, Guarantees of Origin). Link transition goals to corporate climate strategy.
awareness.source: ISO 50001 (2018); IEA (2022), Renewables 2022 Market Report; UN Global Compact- Business Ambition for 1.5ºC

developing.text: Develop a renewable-energy roadmap with clear targets (% of electricity from renewables); implement on-site generation (solar PV, biogas) or long-term PPAs for certified green power. Disclose under GRI 302-1/302-4.
developing.source: GRI 302 (2016); ISO 50009 (2019); RE100 (2023), Technical Criteria for Corporate Renewable Electricity

leading.text: Achieve 100 % renewable electricity or net-zero energy operations verified by third-party certification; collaborate with suppliers to extend renewable adoption across the value chain.
leading.source: GRI 302 & ISO 50001; UN Global Compact-"A Global Compact for Sustainable Energy: A Framework for Business Action" (2011); IEA (2023), Net Zero by 2050 Roadmap

questions.sdg_target: 7.3 – Improve energy efficiency
questions.kpi: Integration of energy efficiency into cost and resource management strategy
questions.question: To what extent has the company integrated, reviewed and improved energy-efficiency measures (e.g., equipment upgrades, process optimization) into its overall business strategy to enhance competitiveness and reduce operational costs?

awareness.text: Analyze energy consumption by cost center and identify inefficiencies in machinery, lighting, and compressed-air systems. Communicate potential cost and productivity gains from energy-efficiency investments.
awareness.source: ISO 50001 (2018); GRI 302 (2016); OECD-Energy Efficiency 2021

developing.text: Integrate energy-efficiency into capital-planning and maintenance strategies, tracking savings trends over time; implement energy audits, high-efficiency motors, and variable-speed drives. Link performance to financial KPIs and disclose ROI and intensity improvements.
developing.source: ISO 50002 (2014); GRI 201 (2016); IEA (2022), Energy Efficiency Market Report

leading.text: Institutionalize continual-improvement cycles under ISO 50001; deploy digital-twin or AI systems for predictive optimization; publish verified savings and productivity gains in sustainability and annual reports.
leading.source: ISO 50001 and ISO 50006 (2014); GRI 302 (2016); "Accelerating clean energy through Industry 4.0: manufacturing the next revolution," (2017)

questions.sdg_target: 7.A – Enhance access to clean energy knowledge
questions.kpi: Employee training and awareness on energy efficiency
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, expanded, and evaluated employee training and awareness programs on energy efficiency and the use of clean or renewable energy technologies?

awareness.text: Launch basic energy-awareness campaigns covering conservation behaviors, shutdown procedures, and responsible use of lighting, HVAC, and machinery. Include energy literacy in onboarding.
awareness.source: ISO 50001 (2018); GRI 404 (2016); ILO- Skills for Green Jobs

developing.text: Provide technical training on energy-management practices and renewable-system operation for maintenance, procurement, and engineering teams; measure participation and learning outcomes.
developing.source: GRI 404-1/404-2; ISO 50015 (2014), M&V of Energy Performance; UNIDO- Industrial Decarbonization

leading.text: Institutionalize ongoing “energy-champion” programs and cross-departmental innovation labs; certify internal experts in ISO 50001; share employee-driven efficiency projects publicly as part of SDG 7 commitments.
leading.source: GRI 404; ILO-"Decent Work in Nature-Based Solutions 2022,"; UN Global Compact-The Net-Zero Standard

questions.sdg_target: 8.3 – Promote circular and inclusive economic models
questions.kpi: Integration of reusable, refillable, or take-back systems
questions.question: To what extent has the company developed, implemented and/or scaled circular business models such as reusable, refillable, or take-bac systems to reduce waste and generate new value streams?

awareness.text: Map packaging/product portfolios to identify reuse/refill/take-back opportunities; assess customer segments and reverse-logistics feasibility; align terminology and principles with ISO 59004 and scan EMF case studies for proven models.
awareness.source: ISO 59004:2024; Ellen MacArthur Foundation (EMF), Reuse: Rethinking Packaging (2019); GRI 306:2020

developing.text: Pilot circular models (e.g., B2B totes, refill-on-the-go, deposit-return); define operational specs, cleaning standards, and reverse logistics; measure performance with ISO 59020 metrics, measuring performance vs baseline and disclose material savings under GRI 301/306.
developing.source: ISO 59020:2024; ISO 18601–18606; GRI 301: Materials; GRI 306: Waste

leading.text: Scale commercially viable reuse/take-back with digital tracking, interoperability, and partner ecosystems; integrate circular revenue lines into strategy and publish verified outcomes (return rates, lifetime turns, avoided waste).
leading.source: ISO 59010:2024; Ellen MacArthur Foundation-Circular economy in practice: Case studies and company examples (2021); OECD (2019)-Business Models for the Circular Economy

questions.sdg_target: 8.4 – Improve resource efficiency and decouple growth from environmental degradation
questions.kpi: Cleaner and more efficient production technologies
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented cleaner or resource-efficient technologies (e.g., low-carbon materials, energy-efficient production lines) to reduce environmental impacts while sustaining growth?

awareness.text: Conduct baseline resource and emissions mapping (energy, materials, water, waste) under ISO 14001; identify hotspots via LCA (ISO 14040/44) and benchmark decoupling potential using UNEP/OECD guidance.
awareness.source: ISO 14001:2015; ISO 14040/14044; UNEP Global Resources Outlook; OECD Eco-Innovation in Industry Enabling Green Growth

developing.text: Deploy cleaner-production and resource-efficiency technologies (high-efficiency motors/VSDs, heat recovery, low-carbon materials); integrate targets and M&V via ISO 50001/50015; disclose results in GRI 302 (Energy), 303 (Water), 305 (Emissions), 306 (Waste).
developing.source: ISO 50001:2018 & ISO 50015:2014; GRI 302/303/305/306; UNIDO/UNEP, Resource Efficient and Cleaner Production (RECP) Programme

leading.text: Institutionalize continuous improvement with eco-design (ISO 14006) and supplier engagement; set science-based, time-bound decoupling targets; verify reductions and publish intensity & absolute metrics.
leading.source: ISO 14006:2020, Ecodesign; UN Global Compact / SBTi corporate guidance; GRI Standards (topic-specific 300/400 series)

questions.sdg_target: 8.2 – Achieve higher productivity through sustainable innovation
questions.kpi: Integration of sustainability-driven innovation into business strategy
questions.question: To what extent has the company integrated and operationalised sustainability-driven innovation (e.g., new bio-based materials, recyclable design, digital process optimization) into its business strategy to enhance competitiveness and market growth?

awareness.text: Embed sustainability criteria in the innovation pipeline and portfolio governance; align definitions, roles, and processes with ISO 56002 (innovation management) and screen opportunities using LCA and circular-design principles.
awareness.source: ISO 56002:2019, Innovation management system; ISO 14040/44 (LCA); ISO 14006 (Ecodesign); Ellen MacArthur Foundation-Circular Design Guide

developing.text: Stand up stage-gates with environmental KPIs (recyclability, bio-based share, carbon/water intensity); use digital tools (LCA, digital twins, AI for process optimization); report R&D and capability-building under GRI 201/404.
developing.source: ISO/TR 56004, Innovation management assessment; GRI 201: Economic performance; GRI 404: Training & Education; OECD Eco-Innovation in Industry Enabling Green Growth

leading.text: Scale market launches that deliver verified sustainability advantages; co-innovate with suppliers/customers; publish revenue share from “sustainable solutions” and third-party-verified impact metrics.
leading.source: ISO 56002; EMF, Circular economy business cases; GRI 2 & 201 disclosures (strategy, economic value)

questions.sdg_target: 8.5 – Achieve full and productive employment and equal pay for all
questions.kpi: Decent work and inclusion programs
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, monitored and improved measures to ensure safe, fair, and stable employment conditions for all workers, including fair pay, working hours, and equal opportunity?

awareness.text: Assess compliance with core labor standards and baseline HR policies (equal pay, non-discrimination, working hours, OSH). Communicate commitments aligned with ILO conventions and GRI disclosures.
awareness.source: ILO C100 (Equal Remuneration), C111 (Discrimination), C1/C30 (Hours of Work), C155 & C187 (OSH framework); GRI 401 (Employment), GRI 403 (Occupational Health & Safety), GRI 405 (Diversity & Equal Opportunity), GRI 406 (Non-discrimination); UN Global Compact, Principles 1–6

developing.text: Implement pay-equity analyses and correction plans; ensure secure contracts and predictable schedules; establish worker participation in OSH per ISO 45001 and provide grievance and remediation channels. Disclose metrics (pay gaps, injury rates, turnover).
developing.source: ISO 45001:2018, Occupational health & safety management; GRI 202-1/405-2 (pay ratio & gender pay information), GRI 403-9/403-10 (OSH outcomes); ILO, Decent Work Indicators

leading.text: Set time-bound targets for equal pay and representation at all levels; adopt living-wage roadmaps; integrate inclusive hiring, apprenticeship, and career-progression pathways; independently assure workforce metrics and publish results.
leading.source: GRI 2 (general disclosures on governance & policies), GRI 401/405/406; ILO, Global Wage Report; Equal Pay guideOECD, Due Diligence for Responsible Business Conduct

questions.sdg_description: Build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and foster innovation
questions.sdg_target: 9.1 – Develop quality, reliable, sustainable, and resilient infrastructure
questions.kpi: Infrastructure enabling closed-loop packaging systems
questions.question: To what extent has the company invested in or collaborated on shared infrastructure (e.g., collection, sorting, or refill systems) that enables circular packaging loops?

awareness.text: Identify infrastructure gaps in packaging recovery, sorting, and refill logistics. Map potential synergies with municipalities, industry associations, or recyclers to support circular flows. Align principles with ISO 59004 and Ellen MacArthur Foundation guidance on reuse systems.
awareness.source: ISO 59004:2024 – Circular economy; Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2021), “Reuse: Rethinking Packaging; UNIDO Global consultations on circular economy 2022-2023

developing.text: Co-invest in or co-manage shared collection, cleaning, and refill facilities; establish traceable reverse-logistics partnerships; disclose progress through GRI 301 and 306 indicators.
developing.source: GRI 301: Materials (2020); GRI 306: Waste (2020); OECD Business Models for the Circular Economy

leading.text: Participate in multi-stakeholder circular infrastructure platforms; develop interoperable refill or deposit-return systems; publicly report system-level material recirculation rates and socio-economic impacts.
leading.source: Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2023), Global Commitment Progress Reports; Global Compact Network Germany-Strategy Guide Circular Economy; ISO 59020:2024 – Measuring circularity performance

questions.sdg_description: Build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and foster innovation
questions.sdg_target: 9.4 – Upgrade all industries and infrastructures for sustainability
questions.kpi: Integration of digital and low-impact production systems
questions.question: To what extent has the company digitalised or modernised and progressively optimised its production infrastructure (e.g., automation, digital monitoring, predictive maintenance) to improve environmental performance and resilience?

awareness.text: Assess current infrastructure age, efficiency, and emissions intensity; build understanding of Industry 4.0’s role in energy/resource optimization through ISO 50001 and UNIDO’s industrial modernization guidance.
awareness.source: ISO 50001:2018 – Energy Management Systems; UNIDO Digital transformation; UNIDO Industrial Energy Efficiency; OECD Inclusive, green and digital transformation

developing.text: Implement automation, sensor networks, and predictive-maintenance tools to cut energy, water, and material losses; carry out periodic performance reviews; integrate performance data into ISO 14001 environmental-management reviews; disclose progress via GRI 302/305.
developing.source: ISO 14001:2015 – Environmental Management Systems; GRI 302: Energy / GRI 305: Emissions (2016); UNEP Promoting resource efficiency

leading.text: Adopt fully digital EMS and real-time environmental-performance dashboards; integrate AI optimization; disclose verified resource-efficiency improvements and emission reductions.
leading.source: ISO 50006:2014 – Energy Baselines and Performance Indicators; Industry 4.0: The Future of Manufacturing - SAP; IEA Digitalisation - Energy System

questions.sdg_description: Build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and foster innovation
questions.sdg_target: 9.5 – Enhance scientific research and upgrade the technological capabilities of industrial sectors
questions.kpi: Collaboration and innovation capacity
questions.question: To what extent has the company participated in collaborative innovation projects (e.g., R&D pilots, public–private partnerships, or innovation clusters) focused on advancing bio-based and circular packaging technologies?

awareness.text: Identify national or regional innovation platforms, clusters, or funding schemes relevant to circular packaging; build awareness of open-innovation benefits using ISO 56002 and UNIDO’s innovation ecosystem resources.
awareness.source: ISO 56002:2019 – Innovation Management Systems; UNIDO Circular Innovation; OECD Policies to Strengthen Resilience of Global Value Chains (2023); OECD Risks and opportunities of reshaping global value chains (2023)

developing.text: Join collaborative R&D or PPP projects; share facilities and data for testing bio-based or recyclable materials; track innovation outputs (patents, prototypes, pilots) and disclose through GRI 203 (Indirect Economic Impacts).
developing.source: GRI 203: Indirect Economic Impacts (2016); Ellen MAcArthur Foundation It’s time for a circular economy; EU/UNIDO (2021), Global Eco-Industrial Parks Programme

leading.text: Co-lead international innovation consortia; license or scale circular-packaging technologies; publish collaborative R&D outcomes and socio-economic impacts in sustainability reports.
leading.source: ISO 56003:2019 – Innovation Partnership Guidance; UN Global Compact-SDG Innovation Accelerator program and the promotion of multi-stakeholder partnerships; OECD (2023), Science, Technology and Innovation Outlook

questions.sdg_description: Build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and foster innovation
questions.sdg_target: 9.a – Facilitate sustainable and inclusive industrialisation
questions.kpi: Inclusion and accessibility in industrial transformation
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, expanded, and monitored inclusive participation (e.g., SMEs, women, local suppliers) in its innovation or production ecosystem for sustainable packaging?

awareness.text: Map supplier diversity and SME engagement in the value chain; communicate the economic and social benefits of inclusive industrial participation referencing ILO and UNIDO guidelines.
awareness.source: ILO (2017), “Women and Men in the Informal Economy; GRI 204: Procurement Practices (2016); UNIDO (2022) Industrial Development Report

developing.text: Implement inclusive-sourcing programs for SMEs, women-owned, or local enterprises; build capacity through supplier training and fair-contracting policies; disclose supplier-diversity metrics in GRI 204-1.
developing.source: GRI 204-1: Proportion of spending on local suppliers; UN Global Compact Target Gender Equality; ILO Decent work in global supply chains

leading.text: Establish long-term partnerships with inclusive suppliers and innovation networks; integrate social-procurement criteria into governance; publish verified socioeconomic impact data and local-employment multipliers.
leading.source: GRI 204 / 405 (Procurement & Diversity); OECD (2022), Responsible Business Conduct; UNIDO Green Industrial Recovery Programme

questions.sdg_description: Reduce inequality within and among countries
questions.sdg_target: 10.2 – Empower and promote the social, economic, and political inclusion of all
questions.kpi: Inclusion of marginalized actors in circular value chains
questions.question: To what extent has the company systematically identified, engaged, and integrated small or underrepresented suppliers, recyclers, or social enterprises into its circular packaging systems?

awareness.text: Map small and underrepresented actors (SMEs, informal recyclers, social enterprises) in your packaging value chain. Build internal awareness of inclusive-procurement benefits and risks of exclusion in circular economies.
awareness.source: GRI 204 (2016), Procurement Practices;UN Global Compact initiatives supply chains, human rights, and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) from (2023) ILO Decent work in global supply chains

developing.text: Adopt inclusive-sourcing criteria favoring SMEs, cooperatives, and underrepresented suppliers; provide training on quality, safety, and traceability; measure local-spending shares under GRI 204-1.
developing.source: GRI 204-1 (Local supplier spending); OECD (2022), Responsible Business Conduct for SMEs; UNIDO (2022), Industrial Development Report

leading.text: Establish long-term partnerships with inclusive suppliers and circular-economy cooperatives; report verified socio-economic impacts (jobs supported, value retained locally).
leading.source: GRI 204 & 405 (Diversity); UN Global Compact, Target Gender Equality Accelerator; Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2021), Circular Economy Case Studies

questions.sdg_description: Reduce inequality within and among countries
questions.sdg_target: 10.3 – Ensure equal opportunity and reduce inequalities of outcome
questions.kpi: Equal participation in environmental programs
questions.question: To what extent has the company established, implemented, and monitored formal mechanisms that enable employees from all roles and backgrounds to propose, review, and influence environmental improvements?

awareness.text: Assess employee-engagement structures for inclusiveness (who can make improvement suggestions). Introduce communication channels for all staff to participate in environmental initiatives.
awareness.source: ISO 14001 (2015), Environmental Management Systems; GRI 403 (2018), Occupational Health and Safety; ILO Workplace cooperation: a practical guide (2022-2023)

developing.text: Create formal suggestion and review systems (environmental committees, innovation portals, cross-functional “green teams”); guarantee representation from all employee groups and collect data on participation rates.
developing.source: ISO 14001 clause 5.4 (participation and consultation); GRI 403-4 (Worker participation in OHS management); UN Global Compact (2023), Principle 6 – Eliminate Discrimination in Employment

leading.text: Institutionalize inclusive innovation councils combining environmental, DEI, and OHS functions; publish engagement statistics and environmental-improvement outcomes generated by employee input.
leading.source: ISO 26000 (2010), Guidance on Social Responsibility; GRI 2-12 (Governance and stakeholder engagement); The 2023 UNIDO Annual Report

questions.sdg_description: Reduce inequality within and among countries
questions.sdg_target: 10.4 – Adopt policies to promote greater equality
questions.kpi: Fair distribution of financial rewards and advancement opportunities
questions.question: To what extent has the company established, applied, and regularly reviewed transparent salary bands, promotion criteria, and performance-based incentives that are accessible to all employees?

awareness.text: Audit pay structures and promotion criteria for transparency; benchmark practices against ILO conventions C100 (Equal Remuneration) and C111 (Discrimination).
awareness.source: GRI 405 (2016), Diversity and Equal Opportunity; ILO Convention 100 (Equal Remuneration, 1951); ILO Convention 111 (Discrimination in Employment)

developing.text: Publish internal pay-band frameworks and promotion policies; provide employees access to performance-evaluation criteria; conduct gender- and diversity-based pay-gap analysis annually.
developing.source: UN Global Compact (2022), Target Gender Equality Accelerator; OECD (2021), Pay Transparency Tools to Close the Gender Wage GapGRI 202-1 (Ratio of standard entry level wage by gender)

leading.text: Institutionalize equal-pay certification or external assurance; link bonuses to sustainability and inclusion KPIs; disclose verified pay-equity results and diversity in leadership.
leading.source: GRI 405-2 (Ratio of basic salary and remuneration of women to men); ILO (2023), Global Wage Report 2022-23; UN Women (2021), Equal Pay International Coalition (EPIC)

questions.sdg_description: Reduce inequality within and among countries
questions.sdg_target: 10.2 – Promote inclusion through cultural awareness and belonging
questions.kpi: Inclusion and sense of belonging within workforce
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, monitored, and continuously improved initiatives that foster inclusion and belonging among employees through structured diversity programs, cultural awareness training, or inclusive workplace policies?

awareness.text: Conduct inclusion-climate surveys; promote cultural-awareness and unconscious-bias training; align internal DEI messaging with the UN Global Compact’s Principle 6 and ILO discrimination conventions.
awareness.source: ISO 26000 (2010), Guidance on Social Responsibility; ILO Convention 111 (Discrimination in Employment); UN Global Compact (2023), Principle 6: Eliminate Discrimination in Employment

developing.text: Establish formal DEI programs and employee-resource groups (ERGs); track participation and satisfaction; provide mentorship and leadership training for underrepresented groups; measure participation and satisfaction rates under GRI 405.
developing.source: GRI 405 (2016), Diversity and Equal Opportunity; UN Women (2022), A Toolkit on Paid and Unpaid Care Work: From 3Rs to 5Rs OECD (2022), Diversity and Inclusion

leading.text: Embed inclusion goals into corporate KPIs; publish annual diversity metrics and inclusion outcomes; obtain external DEI certification or benchmark via recognized indices.
leading.source: ISO 30415:2021 Human Resource Management – Diversity and Inclusion; GRI 2-22 (Statement on sustainability strategy and diversity; UN Women Women’s Empowerment Principles

questions.sdg_description: Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable
questions.sdg_target: 11.6 – Reduce urban waste generation and environmental impact
questions.kpi: Participation in local circular packaging systems
questions.question: To what extent has the company identified, piloted, and scaled collaboration with external stakeholders to establish or support urban packaging take-back, refill, or reuse systems?

awareness.text: Map existing municipal or industry-led collection, reuse, and refill initiatives. Identify where company packaging contributes to urban waste streams and raise awareness among staff and partners about extended producer responsibility (EPR).
awareness.source: Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2021), Reuse: Rethinking Packaging; GRI 306: Waste (2020); UN-Habitat (2021), Waste Wise Cities Programme

developing.text: Collaborate with local governments, recyclers, and community enterprises to pilot refill or take-back systems; establish shared data platforms for packaging recovery and reuse tracking.
developing.source: UNEP (2023), Global Framework on Chemicals (GFC); GRI 301: Materials (2020); OECD (2022), “Extended Producer Responsibility

leading.text: Scale and secure long-term urban reuse and take-back infrastructure through PPPs; co-invest in smart-collection hubs and reverse logistics; publish recovery and reuse metrics under GRI 306.
leading.source: UN-Habitat (2022), Circular Cities and Regions Initiative (CCRI); ISO 59020:2024 – Measuring Circularity Performance; Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2023) Building Prosperity: Unlocking the potential of a nature-positive, circular economy for Europe

questions.sdg_description: Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable
questions.sdg_target: 11.6 – Reduce the adverse environmental impact of cities
questions.kpi: Urban pollution prevention
questions.question: To what extent has the company assessed, implemented, and monitored measures to minimise air, noise, or waste emissions from its urban production or logistics sites?

awareness.text: Assess site-level environmental impacts—emissions, dust, odour, and noise—using ISO 14001 and local regulatory standards; raise employee and supplier awareness on urban environmental health.
awareness.source: ISO 14001:2015 – Environmental Management Systems; GRI 305: Emissions (2016); UNEP and WHO A conceptual framework with special focus on air pollution in African countries

developing.text: Implement mitigation technologies—low-emission vehicles, particulate filters, acoustic barriers, and waste-heat recovery; monitor progress with GRI 305 and ISO 14031 performance evaluation.
developing.source: ISO 14031:2013 – Environmental Performance Evaluation; GRI 306: Waste (2020); Cleaner Production and Resource Efficiency Programme (RECP)

leading.text: Adopt real-time monitoring for air/noise emissions; transition fleet to electric or alternative fuels; publicly disclose verified performance in sustainability reports and ESG indices.
leading.source: ISO 50001:2018 – Energy Management Systems; IEA World Energy Outlook 2023 and the ITF Transport Outlook 2023; UNEP (2023), Global Environment Outlook

questions.sdg_description: Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable
questions.sdg_target: 11.A – Support positive economic, social and environmental links between urban and rural areas
questions.kpi: Local partnerships supporting circular economy
questions.question: To what extent does the company establish economic partnerships with urban micro-enterprises or social cooperatives that strengthen local circular value chains?

awareness.text: Identify opportunities for partnerships with micro-enterprises, informal recyclers, and cooperatives bridging urban and rural systems (e.g., bio-based feedstock collection, packaging recovery).

developing.text: Develop inclusive procurement and micro-supply agreements with local cooperatives; provide training, equipment, or logistics support to strengthen their participation in circular material flows.

leading.text: Integrate urban–rural circular partnerships into long-term sourcing and CSR strategy; monitor socioeconomic impact (income growth, waste reduction) and disclose under GRI 203/204.

questions.sdg_description: Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable
questions.sdg_target: 11.1 – Ensure access to safe and affordable housing and transport
questions.kpi: Worker mobility and wellbeing
questions.question: To what extent has the company identified employee urban-mobility and wellbeing needs and implemented, monitored, and improved workplace measures addressing commuting, safety, and work–life balance?

awareness.text: Assess employees’ commuting, housing, and urban-living challenges; raise awareness of links between mobility, wellbeing, and productivity using ILO and WHO frameworks.
awareness.source: GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety (2018); ILO reports (2022) discuss related topics such as "Decent Work in Nature-based Solutions" and "Decent work in the platform economy," ; WHO healthy workplace framework and model

developing.text: Implement flexible or remote work arrangements, commute-support programs (carpooling, public-transit subsidies, bike storage), and urban-safety audits for all sites.

leading.text: Integrate employee urban-wellbeing indicators into sustainability reporting; collaborate with local authorities for safe transport and community infrastructure; disclose progress annually under GRI 401/403.
leading.source: GRI 401 & 403 (Employment and Health & Safety); WHO (2023) Achieving well-being: a global framework for integrating well-being into public health utilizing a health promotion approach"; ILO (2023), Safe and Healthy Working Environments For All Report

questions.sdg_description: Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns
questions.sdg_target: 12.5 – Substantially reduce waste generation through prevention, reduction, recycling and reuse
questions.kpi: % of total packaging materials designed or recovered for reuse, recycling, or composting
questions.question: To what extent has the company established, monitored, and improved targets and mechanisms to ensure packaging materials are reused, recycled, or composted within a circular system?

awareness.text: Set a baseline for packaging formats and end-of-life pathways; align definitions (reuse, recycling, compostability) with recognized standards and circular principles.
awareness.source: ISO 59004:2024; ISO 18601–18606 (packaging & environment family); EMF (2021), Reuse: Rethinking Packaging

developing.text: Adopt time-bound targets for % reusable, recyclable, or compostable packaging; design to ISO packaging standards, and track diversion under GRI.

questions.sdg_description: Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns
questions.sdg_target: 12.4 – Ensure environmentally sound management of chemicals and waste throughout their lifecycle
questions.kpi: Presence of a chemical and waste management procedure aligned with ISO or GRI frameworks
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, maintained, and improved procedures to manage chemical inputs and prevent their release into the environment across the packaging lifecycle?

awareness.text: Inventory all chemical inputs across printing/coating/lamination; identify substances of concern; embed responsibilities within the EMS.
awareness.source: ISO 14001:2015 — Environmental management systems; UNEP (2023), Global Framework on Chemicals; GRI 303: Water & Effluents (2018)

developing.text: Implement cleaner-production and substitution procedures; set controls for storage/handling and year-to-yea tracking, wastewater pre-treatment, and emission prevention; audit and report.

leading.source: ISO 14046:2014 Environmental management — Water footprint — Principles, requirements and guidelines; EMF Designing out plastic pollution with the circular economy; UNEP — Chemicals & Pollution Action

questions.sdg_description: Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns
questions.sdg_target: 12.6 – Encourage companies to adopt sustainable practices and integrate sustainability information into reporting
questions.kpi: Existence and integration of sustainability performance indicators in financial or management reporting
questions.question: To what extent has the company integrated sustainability performance indicators (e.g., resource efficiency, waste savings, emission reductions) into its financial planning and decision-making processes?

awareness.text: Map material sustainability KPIs to cost drivers (energy, water, materials, waste); establish governance for data quality and decision use.
awareness.source: GRI 2: General Disclosures (governance, policies); ISO 14031:2013 — Environmental performance evaluation; ISO 14051:2011 — Material Flow Cost Accounting (MFCA)

developing.text: Integrate sustainability KPIs into capital budgeting and management reviews; use MFCA and eco-efficiency to link savings and returns; disclose outcomes.
developing.source: ISO 14045:2012 — Eco-efficiency assessment; GRI 201: Economic Performance (2016); UN Global Compact — CFO Principles on Integrated SDG Investments

leading.text: Adopt enterprise-wide dashboards tying resource-efficiency and emissions to P&L and investment decisions; link incentives/bonuses to verified sustainability KPIs.
leading.source: ISO 50001:2018 — Energy management; UN Global Compact- Sustainable Finance; GRI Universal & Topic Standards

questions.sdg_description: Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns
questions.sdg_target: 12.8 – Ensure that people everywhere have relevant information and awareness for sustainable development
questions.kpi: Existence of communication or awareness initiatives on sustainable packaging
questions.question: To what extent has the company defined, implemented, and evaluated communication and awareness initiatives that inform employees, clients, or consumers about responsible packaging use, recycling, or disposal?

awareness.text: Define the priority audiences (operators, sales, customers, end-users); align claims and instructions to recognized guidance and avoid greenwashing.
awareness.source: ISO 14063:2020 — Environmental communication; GRI 417: Marketing & Labeling (2016); UNEP Guidelines for Providing Product Sustainability Information

developing.text: Roll out training and customer-facing materials (how to return/reuse/recycle; composting conditions); monitor reach and comprehension; align with packaging end-of-life standards.

leading.text: Co-create community or customer partnerships that measurably improve correct disposal/reuse; publish behavior-change outcomes over time (return rates, contamination reduction).
leading.source: GRI 306: Waste; UNEP Beat Pollution; UNEP SDG 12 consumption awareness hub;

questions.sdg_target: 13.1 – Strengthen resilience and adaptive capacity to climate-related hazards
questions.kpi: Existence of climate-resilient circular operations (e.g., sourcing, logistics, materials)
questions.question: To what extent has the company assessed, implemented, and maintained adaptations in its circular value chain to withstand climate-related disruptions (e.g. extreme weather, raw-material shortages)?

awareness.text: Map climate-related vulnerabilities in sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, and recycling operations; evaluate exposure to extreme-weather events and resource scarcity.
awareness.source: ISO 14091:2021, Adaptation to climate change; UN Global Compact Climate Adaptation; UNFCCC Global Climate Action Portal

developing.text: Integrate climate-resilience criteria into supplier selection and circular-design processes; diversify sourcing and build redundancy into reverse-logistics networks.

leading.text: Embed adaptive-capacity KPIs (e.g., supply-chain recovery time, climate-risk scoring) into business continuity; disclose in sustainability and resilience reports.
leading.source: ISO/TS 14092:2020 - Adaptation to climate change; GRI 2-12 / 2-22 (2021); UNFCCC Work of the Climate High-Level Champions

questions.sdg_target: 13.2 – Integrate climate measures into strategies and planning
questions.kpi: Existence of a GHG inventory and verified mitigation targets
questions.question: To what extent has the company quantified its greenhouse-gas emissions and established, reviewed, and improved verifiable emission-reduction or neutrality targets?

awareness.text: Establish a full GHG inventory for baseline definition, using the GHG Protocol; understand baseline emissions and data-collection processes.
awareness.source: GHG Protocol (2023); ISO 14064-1:2018, GHG; Science-Based Targets Initiative (SBTi) for Business Ambition 1.5 °C

developing.text: Set near- and long-term, science-based GHG-reduction targets; integrate renewable-energy adoption and efficiency upgrades; disclose per GRI 305.
developing.source: GRI 305: Emissions (2016); ISO 14064-2:2019, GHG; UNEP (2023), Emissions Gap Report 2023

leading.text: Publicly verify inventories and targets via accredited third-party audits; commit to net-zero under recognized frameworks (SBTi Net-Zero Standard).
leading.source: SBTi (2021), Net-Zero Standard; ISO 14068-1:2023 Climate change management — Transition to net zero; UNFCCC Work of the Climate High-Level Champions

questions.sdg_target: 13.2 – Integrate climate-related risks and opportunities into financial planning
questions.kpi: Integration of climate-risk scenarios into strategic and financial planning
questions.question: To what extent has the company assessed, integrated an periodically reviewed climate-related risks (e.g., energy prices, supply chain disruptions, regulation) and opportunities (e.g., green-market access) into its financial or strategic planning?

awareness.text: Identify transition and physical risks using TCFD categories; assess exposure and potential financial implications.
awareness.source: TCFD (2017), Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures; OECD Financial markets and climate transition; PRI | Inevitable Policy Response

developing.text: Integrate TCFD-aligned governance, risk, and opportunity assessments into financial statements; conduct scenario analysis and sensitivity testing.
