leading.text: Align financial disclosures with IFRS S2 (ISSB 2023) and TCFD; publish climate-adjusted ROI and internal carbon pricing; embed resilience metrics in corporate finance.
leading.source: IFRS S2: Climate-related Disclosures; TCFD - Financial Stability Board; UNEP FI- The climate risk tool landscape 2022 Supplement

questions.sdg_target: 13.3 – Improve education, awareness, and capacity on climate mitigation and adaptation
questions.kpi: % of employees trained or engaged in climate initiatives
questions.question: To what extent has the company defined, implemented, and evaluated training or engagement programs that build employee and partner capacity to contribute to climate-mitigation and adaptation actions within their roles?

awareness.text: Develop climate-literacy and awareness campaigns for all staff; explain company climate targets and personal relevance.
awareness.source: UNFCCC (2022), Action for Climate Empowerment (ACE) programme; UN Global Compact-Climate Ambition Accelerator; ILO (2020), Skills for a Greener Future – Global View

developing.text: Offer structured internal and supplier-training on energy efficiency, carbon accounting, and adaptation practices; measure learning outcomes and behavioral change.
developing.source: GRI 404: Training and Education (2016); UNESCO Climate change education for sustainable development; ISO 14001 Clause 7.3, awareness

leading.text: Institutionalize annual climate-competence programs; certify “climate champions”; extend learning to customers and community partnerships; disclose participation metrics.
leading.source: GRI 404-2, Training and Education; UN Global Compact Academy; UNFCCC-Action for Climate Empowerment Hub

questions.sdg_target: 14.1 – Reduce marine pollution from land-based activities
questions.kpi: Presence and maturity of granulate/powder/pellet loss-prevention and stormwater controls
questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented, monitored, and maintained controls to prevent material loss (e.g., pellets, flakes, powders, fines) to drains and stormwater?

awareness.text: Awarenes: Identify potential pathways for plastic or material leakage into water systems; conduct site-level audits of production, transport, and cleaning operations.
awareness.source: UNEP - A Global Assessment of Marine Litter and Plastic Pollution; Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2019), Plastics and the Circular Economy; Operation Clean Sweep (Plastics Europe/ACC)

developing.text: Implement containment controls (filter traps, sealed storage, stormwater grates, pellet-handling protocols); track and report spills or material losses annually.
developing.source: ISO 14001:2015 – Environmental Management Systems; GRI 306: Waste (2020); UN Global Compact-End Waste Entering the Ocean

leading.text: Certify operations under pellet-loss prevention standards; engage in local watershed cleanups and circular redesign to eliminate leakage risk across the value chain.
leading.source: ISO 14063:2020 – Environmental Management; UNEP-Talks on global plastic pollution treaty adjourn without consensus; OCS Blue - Operation Clean Sweep

questions.sdg_target: 14.3 – Minimize and address impacts of ocean acidification
questions.kpi: Implementation of acidifying emissions/effluent monitoring and neutralization
questions.question: To what extent has the company monitored and reduced acidifying emissions or effluents that can alter downstream water pH?

awareness.text: Awarenes: Map sources of acidifying substances (SO₂, NOₓ, acidic effluents); assess local discharge regulations and downstream water vulnerability.
awareness.source: UNESCO-IOC (2021), Global Ocean Acidification Observing Network (GOA-ON); ISO 14001:2015 – Environmental Management Systems; UNEP-Marine and Land-based Pollution

developing.text: Install treatment systems (neutralization, scrubbers, effluent pH correction); monitor discharge pH and buffer capacity; disclose data through GRI 303.
developing.source: GRI 303: Water and Effluents (2018); ISO 5667-10:2020 Water quality — Sampling Part 10: Guidance on sampling of waste water; UNEP - UN Environment Programme's World Water Quality Alliance (WWQA),

leading.text: Publicly report pH-adjustment performance and downstream impact studies; collaborate with research bodies on ocean chemistry; aim for zero-acidification footprint.
leading.source: GRI 305: Emissions (2016); UN Global Compact-The Ocean Stewardship 2030 roadmap: ensuring a healthy and productive ocean by 2030; UN Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development

questions.sdg_target: 14.a – Increase scientific knowledge, research capacity for ocean health
questions.kpi: Budget and collaborations for aquatic-safety R&D (eco-toxicity, fragmentation, microfiber/microplastic risk, water-degradation testing)
questions.question: To what extent has the company, since a defined baseline year, systematically invested in or participated in R&D or partnerships to assess and reduce aquatic impacts of its materials and processes?

awareness.text: Awarenes: Identify research needs regarding aquatic impacts (microplastics, chemical leachates, biodegradability); map external R&D networks and university or NGO partners.
awareness.source: GRI 203: Indirect Economic Impacts (2016); EMF-"Universal circular economy policy goals" and "Circular Economy for Plastics"; UNESCO-IOC United Nations Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development (2021-2030)

leading.text: Co-develop open-access ocean-health databases or biomaterial R&D platforms; disclose funding for marine-research partnerships and eco-design breakthroughs.
leading.source: GRI 203: Indirect Economic Impacts 2016, GRI 301: Materials 2016; UN Global Compact, Sustainable Ocean Principles; UNESCO- United Nations Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development (2021-2030)

questions.sdg_target: 14.1 / 14.a – Reduce pollution via awareness & cooperation
questions.kpi: Share of workforce/partners covered by spill response & water-protection training and incident reporting
questions.question: To what extent has the company defined, implemented, and evaluated training and reporting mechanisms for employees and contractors on spill prevention, stormwater protection, and incident response related to water contamination risks?

awareness.text: Awarenes: Conduct awareness sessions on spill risks, drain mapping, and marine pollution impacts; display clear signage and emergency contacts at operational sites.
awareness.source: GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety (2018); ISO 14001:2015 – Environmental management systems (clause 7.3 awareness); UNEP Chemicals and pollution action

developing.text: Establish spill-prevention and stormwater-management procedures; conduct periodic drills; introduce incident-reporting systems and track corrective actions.

leading.text: Integrate spill-prevention and water-protection training into certification programs; publicly disclose incident data and corrective measures; collaborate with coastal NGOs on water quality.

questions.sdg_target: 15.2 – Sustainably manage forests; halt deforestation / 15.5 – Reduce habitat loss
questions.kpi: Share and maturity of actions that lower reliance on virgin land-sourced biomass (e.g., recycled fibre content, agri-by-products, design that reduces material intensity)
questions.question: To what extent has the company reduced dependence on virgin land-sourced biomass by increasing recycled/secondary bio-based inputs?

awareness.text: Quantify current reliance on virgin vs. recycled/secondary biomass (by mass and spend) to establish a baseline. Align terminology and targets with circular-economy and chain-of-custody standards; screen feasibility of substituting residues and post-consumer fibers for virgin inputs.

leading.text: Prioritize closed-loop specs with recyclers; publish verified % recycled/secondary content and avoided virgin extraction; integrate circularity metrics into product approvals.

questions.sdg_target: 15.2 – Sustainably manage forests; halt deforestation / 15.1 – Conserve terrestrial ecosystems
questions.kpi: Existence and coverage of a deforestation- and conversion-free (DCF) sourcing policy with traceability/certification for plant-based inputs (pulp, starch, etc.)

awareness.text: Awarenwss: Map all bio-based feedstocks to source regions; identify exposure to deforestation, conversion, and soil-degradation risks; align definitions with the Accountability Framework.

questions.sdg_target: 15.3 – Combat land degradation and ensure sustainable use of soils

awareness.text: Awarenwss: Assess nature-related dependencies, impacts, and risks across key commodities; identify potential cost exposures (supply disruption, price volatility, compliance).

awareness.text: Awarenwss: Develop concise biodiversity & land-use training (site risks, material handling, spill/soil protection); link to corporate commitments (no deforestation/conversion, soil conservation).

questions.sdg_target: 16.6 – Develop effective, accountable, and transparent institutions at all levels

questions.question: To what extent has the company implemented and expanded systems for transparent traceability of materials and disclosure of circular design and recyclability information to stakeholders?

awareness.source: ISO 59004:2024 — Circular economy; ISO 22095:2020 — Chain of custody; EMF-The Global Commitment: a common vision for a circular economy
